articleTitle: PIICON 2024 Tutorial
Multi Strategy Approaches for Parameter Estimation of One Diode PV Module
abstract: The growing use of photovoltaic (PV) modules, which acts as a substitute for fossil fuels based energy sources is the main motivation of this study, which aims to meet the dire need for sustainable energy solutions. PV modules have difficulties sustaining efficiency in a variety of environmental settings, despite their potential. In order to address this, the current study involves a one diode model of PV module and different methods are used to determine the PV module unknown parameters (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, a, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ph</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf> and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf>). The unknown parameters are calculated using Dandelion Optimizer (DO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Genetic Algorithm Neural Network (GANN), and Hybrid methods. Performance index based on Mean Square Error is evaluated for the aforementioned methods and compared with PSO, ABC, HHO methods from the literature. I-V curves are plotted for R.T.C. France test system and performance index is calculated for the same. Among all methods, GANN method is efficient in attaining better RMSE by closely matching estimated currents with the experimental currents of the considered test system.

articleTitle: Frequency Adaptive Circular Limit Cycle Oscillator-Based Control and Operation of Dynamic Voltage Restorer
abstract: This paper proposed a circular limit cycle oscillatorbased control algorithm for dynamic voltage restorer to mitigate power quality issues. Dynamic voltage restorer is an affordable device to safeguard sensitive/critical loads from distortion, sag, swell, and supply voltage unbalance. The conventional synchronous reference frame phase locked loop-based control algorithm has limitation under unbalance/distorted grid condition. This limitation is addressed in this paper by extracting the fundamental sequence components from the distorted/unbalanced grid signals using circular limit cycle oscillator frequency locked loop. It offers distinct advantages such as simple, robust, and almost asymptotic stable. MATLAB simulation is employed to implement the proposed control algorithm. The results demonstrated the suggested control algorithm provides satisfactory solution to the above problems.

articleTitle: Integrated Infrastructure Strategy for Sustainable Electrical Vehicles Charging Stations and Transportation Networks
abstract: The adoption of Electric Vehicles(EVs) is growing because of their environment-friendly properties and more efficient, With the increasing shift toward EVs, the need for a robust and well-coordinated charging infrastructure has become critical. The current lack of sufficient Fast Charging Stations (FCS) poses a significant challenge to supporting widespread EV usage. Proper planning of charging stations, both in terms of location and capacity, is essential to accommodate rising EV demand. Complicating this process is the interdependence between Transportation Networks (TN) and Power Distribution Networks (PDN), which requires a unified approach for efficient large-scale EV integration. This paper introduces a coordinated planning approach for integrating EV charging stations within both TN and PDN frameworks. A detailed optimization model is presented to identify the optimal locations and capacities for charging stations based on EV traffic patterns and power network capabilities. The traffic flow across the transportation network is modelled using an unconstrained traffic assignment method, while the PDN is represented through a linearized power flow model. To capture the complex interactions between TN and PDN, the model employs a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework that incorporates constraints from both networks. Through simulations on coupled traffic and power networks, the proposed approach demonstrates its effectiveness in optimizing EV charging infrastructure, facilitating a smoother transition to electric mobility.

articleTitle: Active Damping Control using Virtual Synchronous Generator and Sliding Mode Technique for Solar PV and BES based Isolated Microgrid
abstract: Traditional power generation is experiencing tremendous changes, and renewable-based microgrids emerging to play a vital role in the energy sector change. Though the islanded microgrid lacks inertial support, has extensive control capabilities. Usually, a cascaded control technique with an external virtual synchronous generator (VSG) loop and an inner control loop based on proportional integral (PI) controllers is used to regulate the voltage source converter (VSC) output. This paper presents a robust method sliding mode control (SMC) in the inner loop and VSG based control in the outer loop for active damping of electronically coupled distributed generation (DG) unit. The proposed control technique stabilises the terminal voltage and frequency of the DG unit, while protecting the power-electronic interface from external problems. The suggested control strategy effectively manages the voltage levels and demonstrate a high ability to withstand changes in parameters and load variations. It is found that voltage response and frequency variation using VSG and SMC based control has improved transient behavior than PI controllers. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is explored by conducting extensive research on offline simulation and then on real-time platform. Simulation studies are conducted in the MATLAB/Simulink platform, for which real-time validations are conducted on a real-time simulator based on OPAL-RT.

articleTitle: Behaviour analysis of electric vehicle charging flexibility: A data-driven approach
abstract: This paper delves into the unexplored domain of electric vehicle (EV) flexibility in charging behaviour, employing an analysis of 3365 EV charging sessions. The findings underscore the significance of extracting valuable insights from the aggregated U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) dataset, emphasizing the untapped potential of data analysis in power systems. The innovative methodology involves clustering arrival and departure times to identify distinct charging behaviours. Through a detailed examination of each behavioural cluster, encompassing factors such as arrival, departure, and stay duration times, the study proposes measures and an algorithm to quantitatively assess flexibility utilization. The research explores the applicability of data-driven solutions in real-world scenarios, introducing a behaviour analysis method capable of efficiently categorizing large datasets into user groups, including those utilizing spontaneous charging outlets (SCOs), office charging outlets (OCOs), and home charging outlets (HCOs). Addressing the challenge of obtaining precise datasets, particularly with maximum flexibility, machine learning methods are applied. The paper demonstrates the integration of EVs and different machine learning-based clustering techniques which are compared, utilizing clustering for refining extensive datasets and extracting meaningful data.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Isolated Dual Active Bridge Converter
abstract: Dual active bridge converter (DAB) converter has gain popularity recently because of zero voltage switching and bidirectional power flow. Bidirectional power flow allows Grid to vehicle and Vehicle to grid power flow hence transforming the consumer to a prosumer. Aim of this paper is to compute reliability of DAB converter in terms of failure rate of components of DAB converter. Failure rate of different components of DAB converter have been computed using MIL-HDBK-217F. Also, it has been demonstrated using computed reliability that which component is most important in terms of DAB reliability.

articleTitle: Holistic approach of Dynamic & EMT Study for Black start and Restoration in Co-ordination with Protection Issues
abstract: System restoration following a widespread blackout needs detailed studies while considering several criteria such as the path to be chosen for black start, black start generator AVR capabilities, addition of load quantum in each step, etc. Every aspect needs to be simulated beforehand with proper modelling of all the elements. EMT studies need to be undertaken to understand the voltage rise, self-excitation and other phenomena observed during restoration process. Protection setting changes may also need to be done in these cases to avoid tripping during network synchronization and restoration activities as the network is comparatively very weak. This paper presents a holistic approach of required Dynamic and EMT simulation along with protection consideration for a robust restoration path and streamline this procedure and outline the necessary steps to be undertaken while planning black start and restoration schemes.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Optimal Allocation of DG Unit in Distribution System
abstract: Research on the concept of distributed generation (DG) installation has been primarily driven by the quickly dwindling fossil fuels, the substantial environmental repercussions and Utilities are having severe issues with their power systems as a consequence of the ongoing increase in demand of electricity and the inadequate investment in electrical distribution networks. Distributed generation (DG) is one of the alternative for mitigating load growth, line overloading, and reliability with respect to of equipment maintenance interval exhaustion and line losses. Based on the ideal distribution of DGs, power system analyst and engineer describe their attempts to address the issues with power loss, energy losses, stability of voltage, and voltage characteristics in the distribution system. The present investigation conducts an extensive review of the analytical, numerical, meta-heuristic and hybrid methodologies for distributed generation (DG) placement in order to provide utility engineers the most appropriate information for future progress in this field of work.

articleTitle: IEC 61850 Based Cyber Physical System in Smart Grid
abstract: In the evolving landscape of smart grid (SG) and its technologies, there is a continuous trend towards incorporation of zero-emission technologies. This integration sharpens the SG's and focuses on facilitating two-way communication across the generation, transmission, and distribution sectors. SG systems feature intricate architectures containing smart devices and infrastructures based on the Internet of Things (IoT). The IoT platform within SG possess impressive speed, responsiveness, and reliability. However, it also faces a significant vulnerability to cyber-attacks. The scope of attacks extends beyond communication networks to encompass all elements of the SG connected to the network source. One such vulnerable component is the power system, which is susceptible to attacks. In response to these threats, various standards and protocols have been introduced to counter the cyber-attacks in SG. In this study, IEC 61850 based communication protocols are discussed which are hugely used in cyber physical system. IEC 61850 encompasses crucial protocols such as Manufacture Message Specification (MMS), Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event (GOOSE), and Sampled Values (SV). The study enlightens the cyber physical system within these protocols, aiming to capture the attention of researchers and authors working in the field of cyber-attack detection.

articleTitle: Integration of Solar PV Battery Storage System with Cascaded H-Bridge Multi-Level Inverters for Enhanced Grid Performance
abstract: This paper proposes a grid-connected solar PV system employing a multi-level inverter in a double-stage configuration. The topology consists of two symmetrical cascaded H bridges connected to two solar PV arrays interfaced with the battery energy storage system (BESS). Optimum Power of solar PV arrays is tracked using perturb & observe (P&O) method and power flow from the inverter to grid is attained by implementing the d-q and phase lock loop (PLL) synchronization control scheme. Due to the features of MLI, the output voltage obtained has lower values of harmonic distortion, with lower switching frequency operation, need of bulky filter requirement is reduced and minimum switching losses is achieved resulting in an overall increase in system efficiency. The design, control and simulation results have been validated to verify the effective performance of the proposed system in dynamic and steady state operation using MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Upstream Fault Detection Technique in Grid-Connected EVCS Using Negative Sequence Components
abstract: The widespread integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations into the existing utility grid is causing significant power quality and protection challenges. These challenges are notably impacting load performance for both large and small-scale consumers. As the transition from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to EVs accelerates, driven by their numerous benefits, these issues are becoming increasingly severe. EV chargers rely on power electronics to convert AC power from the grid into DC power for battery charging. However, this conversion process, which involves high-frequency switching converters, generates harmonics that degrade grid current quality. This degradation leads to electrical and thermal stress on distribution transformers, ultimately reducing their operational lifespan. Additionally, there are concerns about increased grid current demand, supply-demand imbalances, and voltage fluctuations. Beyond power quality issues, there is a pressing need to develop fast fault detection algorithms to safeguard EV charging station equipment against faults, whether on the grid side or within downstream DC components. This paper introduces a Q-sum (cumulative sum) of the rate of change of a negative sequence (RCNS) power-based fault detection algorithm designed specifically for grid-connected EV charging stations operating in both G2V and V2G modes.

articleTitle: Maximum Loadability Estimation for Identifying Weak Nodes Using Voltage Stability Indices
abstract: Voltage stability evaluation has become essential for the reliable operation of power systems, particularly under heavily loaded conditions. With rising power demand and the integration of various power sources, precise system operation is paramount. Determining the maximum loadability limit before a potential voltage collapse is crucial for maintaining stability. Early warning systems can prevent overloads by identifying critical stability thresholds. This study investigates the use of voltage stability indices in power systems to approximate maximum load capacity and pinpoint the most vulnerable nodes. Numerical analyses on IEEE 14 and IEEE 30 bus test systems demonstrate the effectiveness of the Fast Voltage Stability Index (FVSI) and Line Stability Index (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</inf>) under normal and high reactive loading conditions. These indices not only identify critical buses but also guide optimal placement of FACTS devices, significantly enhancing the voltage stability margin.

articleTitle: Impedance-Based Stability Analysis and Control of DC Cascaded System
abstract: This article comprehensively analyses the instability associated with constant power loads in DC-cascaded systems. The discussion focuses on the DC cascaded system, which consists of buck and boost converters supplying loads at constant voltage. The system rating is a 200 W buck converter that steps down the voltage from 48 to 24 V, supplying a resistive load and an additional 100 W buck and 30 W boost converter loads. Voltage-mode control is realized using the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller which enhances the DC grid stability. Further, the impedance-based interaction within the system is analyzed. MATLAB and PSIM simulation results are given to validate the analysis in ensuring the system stability under varying load conditions.

articleTitle: Variable-Parameter Field-Oriented Control for Interior-Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Drives
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) are becoming widely considered in many applications, including appliances, manufacturing machinery, medical equipment, military equipment, propulsion systems, servo systems, etc. In IPMSMs, the flux linkage may vary significantly depending on the design and operating conditions, and their accurate modeling and control are essential. Look-up tables (LUTs) may be used to represent the flux-current relationship, which inherits the magnetic-flux saturation and cross-coupling characteristics. This paper presented a variable-parameter (inductance) field-oriented control (FOC) strategy with a feedforward speed loop for IPMSM drives, wherein the LUTs are used to represent the current-flux relationship and update the gains of the PI controllers for better decoupling between the q- and d-axes currents. The simulation studies demonstrate the proposed methodology of the variable-parameter FOC for IPMSMs in the unsaturated and saturated regions and its advantages over the conventional FOC algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Antlion optimizer for ring design in a 400kV Tension insulator
abstract: The key aspects for the reliability of the system include adequacy, resilience, redundancy, preventive maintenance and monitoring. The E-field in a high voltage insulator plays a major role in deciding the hydrophobicity of the material and initiation of partial discharge. Prevention of these situations can be avoided by ensuring proper design of the ring structures. The E-field in the polluted insulators is greatly affected compared to the virgin insulator due to the effect of surface conductivity and formation of dry bands. In this work, the efficacy of the optimized rings of 400kV insulator is verified under the contaminated conditions. The impact of electric field is analyzed for various thicknesses and orientation of the industrial pollutant. The optimized rings perform well under these contaminated conditions, successfully reducing the electric field below corona initiation levels.

articleTitle: Review on Advancements in Bidirectional On-Board Chargers for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The rapid development of electric vehicles presents substantial opportunities to enhance the use of clean energy in the ongoing transformation of the automotive industry. On-Board chargers (OBC) are commonly used in electric vehicles due to their low cost and ease of installation. Limited space and short charging times in the electric vehicle require OBC to be high efficient and power-dense. Moreover, the capacity to feed power back into the grid has generated renewed interest in bidirectional power flow solutions in the vehicle industry. This article shows a detailed overview of the current status of OBC technology, including architectures and configurations, smart modes of operations essential elements, standards in the marketplace, and commercial solutions. It also looks at the most recent developments in bidirectional OBCs, focusing on problems and future trends in topologies, wide band-gap technologies, wireless charging systems, and system integration. A comprehensive study of possible topologies for bidirectional OBCs, including single-phase and double-phase layouts, is provided.

articleTitle: Optimization and Performance Analysis of PMUs Allocation for Identification of Single-Line-to-Ground Faults with Line Break
abstract: Transmission and distribution networks experience greater risk of single-line-to-ground faults with line breakage (SLGFs-LBs). SLGFs have identical source-side electrical properties and operate under distinct distribution network conditions, making them hard to differentiate in resonant and ungrounded grounding systems. This study develops a new distribution network defect detection approach using PSO, GSA and PMU technologies to improve efficiency and reliability. This method optimises PMU placement intelligently and flexibly. SLGFs-LBs are distinguished from SLGFs. Both fault types’ source and load side voltage characteristics are investigated and the phase difference between the failed and non-failed phases on the load side is chosen as the differentiation condition. Simulation studies validate the method’s efficacy and robustness. The proposed technique is intended to detect distribution network issues involving single-line-to-ground faults (SLGFs) caused by line breakage (SLGF-LB). Finally, this technique aims to improve distribution network dependability by enhancing fault identification skills through accurate characterization of flaws.

articleTitle: Determination of short-circuit reactance of transformers from SFRA measurements
abstract: The short circuit reactance of transformers is an accepted parameter for determining the mechanical integral of the windings. It is usually measured in the factory during load loss measurements. SFRA (Sweep Frequency Response Analysis) measurements carried out in the end-to-end short circuit mode have the same measurement configuration as that of load loss. Hence, a novel method for determination of short-circuit reactance from SFRA measurements is presented in this paper. The method is validated by field measurements on transformers belonging to different vector groups.

articleTitle: Fault Classification in Transmission Lines Using Radial Basis Function Neural Networks
abstract: Fault classification in transmission lines is essential for maintaining a stable, efficient, and safe power supply, which is fundamental to modern society’s functioning and economic well-being. The wavelet transform-based techniques have limited performance for fault detection and classification in transmission lines since they rely on threshold limits. Since, the core issue is that the optimal threshold value depends on the specific power system network, making it difficult to establish a universal threshold for accurate fault classification. This research article proposes the use of a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) with wavelet transform for fault detection and classification in transmission lines. This study investigates the challenge of threshold selection in wavelet transform-based fault detection techniques, highlighting that RBFNNs do not require pre-defined thresholds for fault identification. The paper also emphasizes the importance of extensive training and testing data to achieve high accuracy. This approach offers a promising alternative to traditional wavelet transform methods by eliminating the need for network-specific threshold selection.

Author Keywords: Neural network and Radial basis function

articleTitle: Eight Switch Converter: A Novel Alternative for Combined Three Phase and Single Phase Loads
abstract: This paper proposes an eight-switch converter for simultaneous balanced three-phase and single-phase outputs/inputs that is derived from the nine-switch converter with the goal of reducing costs. Depending on the phase difference between its two terminal sets, the nine-switch converter's maximum achievable amplitude at its outputs is subject to certain limitations. Nonetheless, it is demonstrated that the nine-switch converter favorably improves the system's overall power quality with a well-designed control structure, supporting its use as a power converter at a lower semiconductor cost. In addition to having fewer switches than a traditional back-to-back converter (eight instead of twelve), the eight-switch converter has good interfacing and integration capabilities for renewable energy sources and can improve voltage and frequency regulation of the suggested system. The entire system of eight switch converter has been modelled and simulated using Matlab/Simulink, the necessary control algorithm for the proposed converter configuration has been discussed in details and the proposed system is verified using OPAL RT 4510 real time simulator.

articleTitle: Power System Inertia Forecasting Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly wind and solar, has introduced substantial challenges to the stability of power systems due to their inherently low inertia, leading to fluctuations in system frequency. Frequency containment reserves are crucial for counteracting these fluctuations, but their effective deployment relies heavily on accurate inertia forecasts. Several forecasting models like time series, machine learning, and deep learning are used for inertia forecasts. Deep learning models show superior performance among these models. However, a single deep-learning model may not offer the desired accuracy. Also, the deep learning model’s accuracy highly depends on its hyperparameters. This necessitates hybrid deep learning models where one or two deep learning models will be combined. Also, effective hyperparameter tuning necessitates a suitable optimization algorithm. Therefore, this paper proposes a hybrid deep-learning model (CNN-GRU-BO) using two deep-learning algorithms: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) models. The hyperparameters of the proposed model are optimized by Bayesian Optimization (BO). The CNN model is proficient in extracting spatial features, while the GRU model excels at capturing temporal dependencies from the data. The BO ensures the optimal configuration of the hyperparameters. The performance of the CNN-GRU-BO model is compared with different reference models. The results show that the CNN-GRU-BO model outperforms the reference models.

articleTitle: An Indirect Current Vector Controlled 3-level VSC fed Induction Motor Driven EV under Extra Urban Driving Cycle
abstract: In this paper, an experimental setup of 3-phase voltage source converters (VSCs) fed induction motor (IM) drive and MATLAB Simulink real-time interface (RTI) model of indirect current vector control (ICVC) scheme is presented. The presented ICVC scheme for VSC fed IM drive is validated through dSPACE CLP1104 real-time controller. In view of electric vehicle (EV) application, the ICVC based IM drive is tested on the extra urban driving cycle (EUDC). The EUDC performance of IM drive is presented through the recorded results on digital storage oscilloscope.

articleTitle: Airport Microgrid Stability Enhancement Using ITAE-Based PID Controller
abstract: The microgrid is a set of various small-scale generating and storage units. In this article, frequency deviation of airport microgrid (AμGd) system is controlled using integral-time-absolute-error (ITAE). In AμGd architecture, storage and generating units along with the loads are taken into consideration. As a key feature, aircraft and the electric vehicles present at the airport are also integrated into the AμGd architecture. All components are modeled into the transfer function of first order. The combined transfer function for the AμGd is obtained and approximated into FOPDT model. Further, ITAE tuned PID controller is applied for the improvement of frequency deviation. Responses for frequency deviation are plotted before and after the controller implementation. Time and frequency domain specifications are also tabulated for the performance indices analysis. Obtained results support the validation of implemented control strategy to mitigate frequency deviation.

articleTitle: Advanced Pumped Storage Hydropower Technologies for Enhanced Grid Stability and Flexibility
abstract: This work provides a comprehensive analysis of the modelling and dynamic characteristics of various Pumped Storage Hydropower (PSH) technologies, namely Fixed-Speed (FS), Variable-Speed (VS), and Ternary (T) PSH systems. We utilize MATLAB/Simulink to construct and simulate these models in order to evaluate their efficiency in frequency regulation and load balancing across different grid scenarios. The study uncovers important information about the operational benefits and constraints of each PSH technology, offering essential data for enhancing grid stability and performance.

articleTitle: Smart Charging for Electric Vehicles in G2V and V2G modes
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are gaining more and more popularity in today’s world due to their exceptional advantages. Effective planning is required to carry out EV charging smoothly, as the random charging process could lead to problems like transformer overloading and increased feeder energy losses. The proposed work includes the implementation of a G2V scheme for smart charging of vehicles with charging cost minimization and V2G technology into the distribution network to support grid voltage. An IEEE 33 bus distribution network is used as the test system for evaluating the proposed smart charging strategy. The main objective is to minimize the overall charging costs for EVs. It is done by developing an objective function that considers various cost factors associated with EV charging. Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology is incorporated into the system to allow EVs to discharge energy back to the grid when needed. This bi-directional energy flow supports grid voltage regulation and enhances the overall stability of the distribution network. Linear programming is employed to solve the objective function. This mathematical approach is chosen for its effectiveness in handling linear constraints and objective functions, ensuring an optimal solution for cost minimization.

articleTitle: Active Equalization and Cell Balancing Circuits for Battery Management System: An Overview
abstract: Battery management system (BMS) plays an important role in ensuring safe and efficient operation and long-term liveliness of the battery over thousands of charging cycles. Active equalization and cell balancing are crucial aspects of the BMS in electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy sources (RESs) with energy storage systems (ESSs), and portable electronics. Generally, active equalization and cell balancing circuits are divided into transformer-based, inductor-based, capacitor-based, and converters-based circuits. Also, these active equalization circuits can be categorized into different categories, such as direct cell-to-cell (DC2C), adjacent cell-to-cell (AC2C), pack-to-cell (P2C), cell-to-pack (C2P), and any cell to any cell (AC2AC), based on their energy transfer methods. This paper provides an overview of different types of active equalization and cell balancing circuits for the BMS for both stationary as well as dynamic ESS applications. Then, the challenges and limitations associated with these active equalization circuits have been discussed. Finally, these active equalization and cell balancing circuits have been compared and summarized in terms of size, control, speed, and efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Economic Analysis of a Hybrid Power Supply System for Mission Critical Applications
abstract: Hybrid power supplies that utilize renewable energy sources have emerged as pivotal solutions to ensure uninterrupted power for critical applications such as telecom towers in remote regions. This paper evaluates the feasibility and efficacy of a hybrid power supply integrating a liquid propane (LP) generator, Battery Energy Storage (BES), and Photovoltaic Panel (PV). The study investigates the fuel efficiency of the LP generator with a hybrid system incorporating BES and BES combined with PV across diverse loading conditions and temperatures. Furthermore, it conducts a comparative analysis of the total cost of ownership between a direct LP system and hybrid systems equipped with BES and PV panels. Simulation results conducted via an Excel spreadsheet underscore that the hybrid PV system achieves superior fuel efficiency and monthly fuel savings when the LP generator operates at 80% rated capacity compared to 60% rated capacity. During a 20-year span, the hybrid PV system with the LP operating at 80% rated capacity produces significant savings of $335,912.48 compared to the direct configuration of the LP generator.

articleTitle: Optimal Zonewise Allocation of EV Fast Charging Stations in IEEE Distribution Systems Using Walrus Optimizer
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are gaining more popularity because of their positive environmental impact and improvements in battery technology. Nevertheless, the extensive use of EVs creates major difficulties for the existing electric power infrastructure, particularly affecting distribution systems. A key factor is strategically positioning EV charging stations within distribution networks to optimize operation while minimizing effects on system stability and reliability. The random placement of EV charging stations affects the voltage profiles and increases overall power loss in the distribution network. As a consequence, the overall quality of the power decreases. The primary aim of this paper is to optimally locate the electric vehicle charging stations in the existing radial distribution network while considering real power losses and the voltage at the system's buses. This optimization problem is solved using the Walrus Optimizer (WaO), a nature-inspired optimization method. In reducing active power loss and voltage deviations in distribution systems with integrated EV charging stations, WaO surpasses other contemporary optimization methods. The findings indicate that the suggested approach is more efficient for integrating electric vehicle charging stations into the distribution network.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow in Presence of Wind Generation Using Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm
abstract: paper introduces an artificial hummingbird algorithm (AHA) to solve the optimal power flow (OPF) in the presence of wind generation. The wind velocity is modelled using Weibull probability distribution function (PDF) and Monte-Carlo simulation method is used to calculate the uncertainty cost of wind power generation. The objectives of this stochastic OPF problem are minimizing the total generation cost including the cost for thermal generation and the uncertainty cost of wind power generation, minimizing active power loss, and voltage magnitude deviation. A penalty-based constraint handling method is used to tackle different constraints of the OPF problem. The proposed algorithm has been tested on the IEEE 30-bus test system, and the system has been modified by the addition of a wind farm to one of the load buses. The outcomes that are achieved using AHA is compared with grey wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm. The comparison shows the supremacy of the artificial hummingbird algorithm (AHA) over GWO algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
abstract: In response to global climate change, the energy landscape is undergoing a major transformation. To reduce dependence on fossil fuels and limit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, renewable energy sources like solar, wind, and geothermal are increasingly being adopted. Countries such as Singapore are shifting away from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles toward electric vehicles (EVs) to foster a more sustainable energy future. As the adoption of EVs grows, ensuring sufficient availability of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) becomes crucial, highlighting the need to optimize their placement and sizing. This paper presents an approach for optimizing the placement of EVCS within the IEEE-33 Bus system. The system is divided into five distinct regions to accommodate varying load requirements based on different load types. Using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, the optimal placement of EVCS is determined, assuming two cars per AC charger and one car per DC charger. Three scenarios are analyzed, with results showing that as EV penetration rates and numbers rise, total power losses and voltage deviations in the system also increase. However, the application of PSO effectively minimizes these power losses and deviations, demonstrating the algorithm’s ability to enhance overall system performance.

articleTitle: Pole-placement Based Controller Design for High Gain Quadratic Boost Converter
abstract: This work presents a controller design method for load voltage regulation of an enhanced gain quadratic type boost converter (EQBC) reported in literature. Firstly, the small-signal model defining the quadratic topology dynamics evolved, and then the control-to-output transfer function (COTF) is formulated. Detailed pole-zero analysis of COTF revealed that two dominating complex conjugate pole-pairs near the jω-axis determine the dynamic response and its specifications. In addition to complex conjugate pole-pairs, it contains non-minimum phase zeros which are responsible for sluggish speed of response. A single-loop voltage-mode type compensator employing a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller is designed to control the load voltage using the dominant pole-placement technique. Dominance factor of 3 is used to place the poles at the desired locations. The efficacy of the proposed design is validated by considering a 24 to 100 V EQBC converter system. At first, the analytical design results are generated; subsequently, their validity is confirmed through the results obtained from the power electronic circuit simulator.

Author Keywords: Enhanced gain quadratic type boost converter

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation and Validation of Suitable Control Algorithms to Improve Power Quality of a PV-Integrated Distribution System
abstract: The increasing integration of distributed generation (DG) systems, specifically photovoltaic (PV) systems, into the grid makes power quality maintenance a critical concern. Shunt active power filters (SAPFs) have emerged as effective solutions for mitigating power quality issues such as harmonic distortion and reactive power imbalance. This paper presents a comparative study of various control techniques employed for PV-integrated SAPF in grid-connected DG systems. The study aims to evaluate the performance of different control strategies in terms of efficiency, reliability, and harmonic compensation capability. The investigated control algorithms include three prominent harmonic compensation theories: instantaneous active and reactive power theory, synchronous reference frame theory, and instantaneous symmetrical component theory. Simulation studies are conducted using MATLAB/Simulink to assess each control technique’s dynamic response and harmonic compensation performance under various operating conditions. Also, the control techniques have been validated in a laboratory prototype test setup. The results provide valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of each control strategy, aiding in the selection of an optimal control algorithm for PV-integrated SAPFs in grid-connected DG systems.

Author Keywords: Instantaneous active and reactive power theory (PQ)

articleTitle: Optimal Location and Impact Analysis of Fast Charging Station on Distribution System
abstract: The public transportation sector contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions, leading to increased carbon levels and global temperatures. Electric Vehicles (EVs) have become a promising solution to reduce pollution and reliance on fossil fuels. Despite efforts to convert Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles to electric, the conversion rate remains low, and the availability of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) is limited. This necessitates the expansion of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure (EVCI), which is accessible to the general populace. The increasing number of electric vehicles emphasizes the need for public EVCI to facilitate the adoption of electric vehicles and provide efficient charging options for electric vehicle owners. To meet the growing demand for electric vehicles, EVCIs must offer fast charging capabilities with multiple Charging Outlets (COs), although this can result in more traffic at charging stations. It results in an increased load of EVCS on the Distribution System (DS), which requires optimal placement of EV load to mitigate voltage deviation and power loss. Therefore, the optimal allocation of the charging station algorithm with varying capacities is proposed using stochastic optimisation techniques at strategic locations within the DS to minimise power loss and voltage deviations. The proposed approach ensures an efficient, reliable, and scalable charging infrastructure, supporting the increasing adoption of EVs and enhancing the overall stability of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Flexibility Dispatch in Distribution Systems considering TSO-DSO coordination
abstract: Distribution Networks with high DER integration can provide energy and ancillary services to the Transmission Network under an appropriate coordination scheme. The distribution system operator(DSO) coordinates with the transmission system operator(TSO) with aggregated bids/offers to sell/buy energy and capacity. The DSO receives an activation signal from the TSO to dispatch the acquired capacity after clearing the energy markets. In this paper, a flexibility dispatch problem is solved to analyze the participation of DERs in providing ancillary services under a hierarchical coordination scheme. After clearing the energy market, the DSO solves a Second Order Conic Programming(SOCP) based Optimal Power Flow(OPF) to dispatch DERs offering competitive prices. A multi-period OPF based on current market timelines is formulated to consider the ramp limits of DERs. Case studies are carried out on the IEEE 33 bus radial network to show the results.

articleTitle: Investigations on Droop Control for Stable Transitions Between Islanded and Grid Operations in Microgrids
abstract: This paper investigates parallel inverter architectures in grid-connected PV systems, focusing on utilizing a droop control strategy (P-ω and Q-E) to enhance active and reactive power sharing. The objective is to ensure stable voltage and frequency in isolated and grid-connected modes in microgrid configurations, which include two PV-connected inverter units of different ratings, a 3-φ load, and a grid. This paper is particularly relevant for implementation in remote villages where solar-tied parallel inverter systems are utilized. The proposed control strategy is also extended to the parallel-connected inverter units. According to this method, no communication channel needs to be established between inverter units, and it offers a prominent solution for areas with multiple PV sources. Along with MPPT, the proposed system optimizes power-sharing. Regulation of voltage and frequency during varying loads in both islanded. Grid-tie modes further justify this control methodology as an engineering solution to improve the performance of parallel-connected solar PV systems. Simulated results validate the robustness of the control methodologies presented here.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Swing Protection for IBR integrated Power Systems based on Impedance Trajectory Tracking
abstract: Extensive integration of inverter based resources on the existing power systems considerably alters the power swing characteristics. Conventional power swing blocking relays fails to detect faster power swings caused by wind generation plants due to decreased system inertia. The impacts of integration of converter interfaced renewable plants like wind plants on conventional power swing protection schemes is analysed. The work proposes a new adaptive power swing protection methodology based on apparent impedance trajectory tracking. This method utilizes the inherent characteristics of apparent impedance trajectory during power swings to discriminate faults and power swings. Modelling and simulations are done using PSCAD/ EMTDC software on IEEE PSRC WG-D6 test system. The proposed method enhances the reliability of distance relays during power swing conditions.

articleTitle: Analyzing Distribution System Hosting Capacity: Impact of EV integration
abstract: A thorough assessment of the distribution lines’ maximum load hosting capacity is required to with stand the increasing load demand. Before undertaking any efforts to reinforce the conductors or cables, it becomes imperative to determine the system’s inherent capacity to support extra load. To ensure that the line’s maximum loading capacity is fully utilized, this strategy plays a crucial role. The primary goal of this study is load growth consideration in terms of residential Electric Vehicles (EVs). It analyzes the effects of increasing load as well as the hosting capacity of the distribution lines to tolerate such an increase as the rolling out of EV’s. The inclusion of renewable penetration has also been considered. This kind of hosting capacity analysis would help consumers and the system operators to investigate the effects, and better prepare for grid operations in the near future. This has been examined for initial configuration of IEEE 33 bus system.

articleTitle: Impedance Matching Method for Fault Location Identification on Three Terminal Transmission Line
abstract: This paper presents an application of new impedance matching based fault location identification method on three terminal transmission network. The voltage and current phasors from the three terminals of the transmission network are considered for calculating fault location on the transmission line. Initially the section on which fault occurs on the three terminal transmission line is identified and then the accurate fault location is identified. The proposed method is independent of transmission line parameters. The proposed method is tested for different faults on different sections of the transmission network and the efficiency is also tested for various source impedances and fault resistances. Further the tentative value of the fault resistance can also be obtained with the proposed method. A three terminal transmission network is considered for simulation studies which is modelled in PSCAD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software and the algorithm is implemented in MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>.

Author Keywords: Prefault and during fault voltage and current phasors

articleTitle: Real-time simulation of Blockchain-Enabled Protection Scheme for DC Microgrids
abstract: This paper presents a novel protection scheme for bipolar DC microgrids, utilizing blockchain technology to enhance security and reliability. An Ethereum-based blockchain network is simulated to ensure the secure transmission of current measurements at the two terminals of the protected DC line. The DC microgrid is simulated in the real-time digital simulator (RTDS), and the measured currents at the remote end of the protected line segment are received through socket protocol (GTNET SKT) using the Python script. The blockchain’s decentralized and immutable nature eliminates single points of failure and provides robust protection against tampering. A user dashboard is also developed for real-time monitoring and visualization of communicated data and blockchain transaction status, facilitating user interaction and system management. Extensive simulations validate the proposed scheme and demonstrate its effectiveness in the security of communication-assisted protection schemes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Transient and Steady State Behaviour of Fault Response with Different Grounding Strategies in Zonal DC Microgrid
abstract: DC microgrids incorporating renewable energy generation and loads are widely discussed, yet they still harbor unresolved safety concerns from a microgrid standpoint. A comprehensive understanding of various grounding strategies is vital for effectively operating and safeguarding the grid. DC microgrid exhibits many more complications in the implementation of the grounding configuration than AC. Therefore, this paper explores and compares the distinct characteristics of the utilized grounding configurations and their specific impacts, particularly focusing on the protection aspects of the DC microgrid which is tested with the MATLAB Simulink by creating a 380V zonal DC microgrid including battery energy storage system (BESS), PV system and different loads. The effects of the different grounding strategies on the DC side of the system are encompassed in the study, with the behavior of all configurations being evaluated in normal working mode and under DC line-to-ground fault conditions, thereby highlighting the LG fault response for different scenarios by analyzing transient and steady-state behavior.

articleTitle: Improved Frequency Control Using Grid Forming Converters in a Multi-Machine System
abstract: This paper addresses the enhancement of frequency stability in electric power systems through the utilization of Grid-Forming Converters (GFMs). As Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) become increasingly prevalent, traditional voltage and frequency control strategies that rely on synchronous generators face significant challenges. The limitations of conventional Grid-Following Converters (GFLs) underscore the necessity for IBRs to mimic synchronous generator behavior, a need effectively met by GFMs.This study explores the integration of GFM technology into the Western System Coordinating Council (WSCC) 9-bus system, employing a Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) based control design to achieve frequency regulation and enhance the system's frequency stability profile.

articleTitle: An Improved Carrier Based PWM Technique to Reduce Neutral Point Voltage Oscillation and CMV of Three Level NPC Inverter
abstract: The power electronic converters, specially the three level neutral point clamped inverters (3LNPCI), which interfaces the renewable power generation to the grid or load, have two main problems, 1) balance of neutral point voltage (NPV) on the DC side 2) the common mode voltage (CMV). It is required to maintain the NPV in a 3LNPCI to minimize the voltage stress on the converter switches and reduce the output voltage harmonics, at the same time the reduction of CMV is also necessary to eliminate the leakage current, otherwise it causes safety issues. There are basically two modulation techniques to operate the power electronic converters, 1) carrier based approach of pulse width modulation (PWM) 2) space vector based approach of PWM. This paper proposes a modified carrier based PWM strategy which is based on the inclusion of a zero sequence voltage and is able to reduce the NPV oscillation and the CMV. The attractive features of the proposed PWM scheme compared to space vector based PWM are, 1) it is easy to calculate and implement on a digital platform 2) reduced switching loss 3) able to reduce the NPV oscillation 4) reduced CMV. A detailed analysis of the proposed modified carrier based PWM scheme is presented. Simulation comparison based results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed PWM strategy.

articleTitle: A Time-Series Decomposition Based Load Forecasting Technique
abstract: Technological advancements in electricity load forecasting (LF) have led to considerable progress from traditional time-series forecasting methods to various deep learning techniques. This broadening of scope is crucial for power system scheduling, planning and maintenance of power systems. In this article, a time-series decomposition-based method known as Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) method is integrated with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for LF. EEMD is used to decompose the time-series load data into various modes. The most relevant decomposed modes, which are directly related to the load data, are extracted out and used to train LSTM network along with the original load data and weather-related information. The forecasting process is conducted using MATLAB version 2021a, utilizing a dataset from Panama City that contains information of electricity load consumption (in MW) along with meteorological parameters such as temperature, rainfall and humidity. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed method, accuracy is assessed in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Root Mean Absolute Error (RMSE).

articleTitle: Challenges And Issues In LVRT Control Strategies For Grid-Interfaced PV Systems: A Brief Review
abstract: The increasing integration of grid-tied photovoltaic (GTPV) systems necessitates frequent updates to grid codes by grid managers to ensure these systems support the safety of the grid. A critical aspect of this is the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability of PV inverters, which allows them to stay connected during short-term grid voltage disturbances. To comply with grid codes, PV inverters incorporate control strategies that ensure smooth operation during LVRT events. However, challenges such as phase voltage imbalance at the point of common coupling (PCC), current distortion, overvoltage in healthy phases, oscillations in active/reactive power and DC-link voltage, inverter overcurrent, and poor dynamic response have been identified during reactive power injection under LVRT conditions. This research examines current issues and strategies related to LVRT in GTPV inverters. It also discusses the limitations of traditional current control strategies and voltage support strategies and categorizes advanced LVRT control approaches based on grid-inverter synchronization methods, current reference generation techniques, and DC-link voltage control under various grid faults.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of Short Circuit Faults in Unbalanced Microgrid System
abstract: The integration of distributed generation and the development of smart grids have increased the occurrence of short-circuit faults in unbalanced microgrid (MG) networks. This Paper provides an accurate and useful time domain short-circuit analysis (SCA) for evaluating these faults. This analysis produces results to analyze the impacts of various fault types by looking at changes in bus voltages, fault current and supply current during fault circumstances. This approach is particularly suited for microgrid technology, where rapid and precise fault analysis is essential for real-time and self-healing operations. Time domain simulation has been applied on a 37-bus test system and the results are obtained for various types of faults. The time-domain analysis of short-circuit faults is conducted using PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Specification Based Fractional Controller for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell
abstract: The primary objective of this manuscript is to suggest analytical tuning rules for controlling the air supply pressure in a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). The controller is designed to effectively regulate the airflow from the supply manifold (SM) to the cathode electrode. Analytical tuning rules are employed to design a novel target loop based fractional control scheme to achieve specific maximum sensitivity (M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) and phase margin (ϕ). The proposed fractional control technique is evaluated against other recently published integer and fractional-order control techniques. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design yields a favorable response compared to existing designs, effectively maintaining the pressure in the supply manifold (SM). The suggested controller’s robustness is examined by introducing 20% perturbations in process gain, delay, and both gain and delay. Quantitative performance analysis is conducted using metrics such as integral square error (ISE), integral time absolute error (ITAE), and integral absolute error (IAE), as well as the integral of the square of the control signal (ISU). Furthermore, the performance of the proposed approach is also verified under varying time delays and sinusoidal disturbances, yielding a similar response.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Battery Current Dynamics in Grid-Connected Electrical Vehicles
abstract: The transition towards sustainable transportation necessitates a thorough understanding of the interaction between Electric Vehicles (EVs) and the distribution grid, especially concerning environmental and sustainability challenges. One critical aspect of this interaction is the behaviour of battery current during the charging and discharging processes. This paper analyses the battery current characteristics in a grid-integrated EV system powered by lithium-ion batteries. The system includes critical components such as a Battery Management System (BMS), a bidirectional propulsion drive, a DC-DC converter (rated at 2.3 mH and 40A), an induction motor for propulsion (3.5/3 kW), and a front-end converter (FEC) integrated with a load emulator. Through experimental investigation, the study reveals significant findings regarding the relationship between reference torque and motor operation modes. Positive reference torque corresponds with the induction machine’s motoring mode, while the propulsion motor’s regenerative mode correlates with energy recovery during deceleration. A critical observation is the impact of abrupt speed variations, which lead to rapid battery depletion. These effects are closely examined under different operational scenarios, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of EV systems. The results highlight the importance of understanding battery behaviour in real-time conditions, which is essential for optimizing EV performance and enhancing grid integration.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Grid Integrated Photovoltaic, Battery and Fuel Cell Hybrid Power System
abstract: This study presents an approach for energy management and system optimization in a hybrid system that includes a fuel cell, battery, and solar system. Determining the ideal configuration for the system’s component parts is the aim of optimization in order to achieve an economically efficient system. The EMS’s (Energy Management System) objective is to regulate the power distribution of system components in order to meet load demand while adhering to other limits. The scheme is to develop and implement a hybrid AC and DC microgrid that utilizes hydrogen storage as a complementary energy source alongside photovoltaic technology (PVT). A bidirectional converter will ease the link between the AC and DC networks that comprises of this microgrid. The research done has an emphasis on the integration of systems and the designing of controllers in order to facilitate the management of electricity in Microgrid system that is connected to the main power grid. A two-tier control system is put up, with a supervisory controller, that keeps the power balance between the dynamic load demand, hydrogen-based energy storage (fuel cell), and intermittent photovoltaic generation. PV system, fuel cell unit and battery system are additionally controlled locally.

articleTitle: Mixed Integer GAO Based Fuzzy Dynamic Braking For Transient Stability Enhancement
abstract: Braking resistors play a crucial role in dissipating excess energy during disturbances, preventing instabilities in the synchronous machines. This paper presents robust approach that integrates a braking resistor with an advanced fuzzy logic controller with genetic algorithm optimisation (GAO). To enhance the functionality of braking resistor, a fuzzy logic controller is employed. However, design of fuzzy controller is trial-and-error based, which can be time-consuming and tedious. To overcome this and further refine the controller’s performance, genetic algorithm is integrated to optimize the tuning of membership functions and control rules. By exploring the solution space, the algorithm ensures optimal performance of the fuzzy controller. The proposed system is simulated in MATLAB, with results highlighting the effectiveness of the controller and substantial improvements in stability.

articleTitle: Level Doubling Network Based Multilevel Inverter for STATCOM Application
abstract: The Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) is a well-known Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS) device utilized in power grids to handle varying conditions. This paper introduced a Cascaded H Bridge Level Doubling Network based Static VAR Compensator (LDN-CHB-STATCOM) with different floating capacitor voltages. The asymmetric topology with a 1:5 asymmetry ratio is used to achieve high-resolution output while maintaining low converter losses. Additionally, reactive power flow control is implemented through the decoupled current control. The paper discusses the transition from reactive power injection to absorption using a proper closed-loop control, ensuring that capacitor balancing and power quality are not affected. Voltage stability and system reliability can be improved by STATCOMs employing LDN-based MLIs to quickly and precisely adjust reactive power. The concept is verified using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Fail Safe Control Strategy For Torque Safety Of Electric Vehicles
abstract: As the electric vehicles (EVs) continue to incorporate more electrical and electronic components, the potential for component failures, leading to unintended torque generation, has increased. This paper explores a fail-safe control strategy designed to address unintended torque generation due to failures in the powertrain’s electrical components. The study systematically identifies and categorizes potential faults in the EV powertrain’s current and position sensors. This paper presents corresponding safety mechanisms and fault mitigation strategies. Through simulation, faults are introduced into the system to evaluate their effect on torque and results shows the effectiveness of implemented safety mechanisms in making the system fail safe.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Performance Evaluation of Surface Permanent Magnet Brushless Motor for Heavy-Duty Electric Vehicles
abstract: The design, finite element analysis and performance evaluation of a surface Permanent Magnet Brushless (PMBL) motor intended for heavy-duty electric vehicles are presented in this paper. Surface PMBL motors are renowned for their strong performance, high efficiency, and power density, which makes them perfect for such applications. A 136 kW, 2000 rpm surface PMBL motor for heavy-duty electric vehicles is designed by assuming various design variables viz. specific magnetic loading, slot-loading, aspect ratio, split ratio, stacking factor, conductor packing factor, current density etc. The CAD program is written for the sizing and performance evaluation. In-depth simulations are carried out using finite element analysis (FEA) to validate the sizing. The results of FEA are compared with the CAD output. The results of FEA are fairly in line with the CAD results. The comparison proves the correctness of the CAD program and validates the design.

articleTitle: QFT Based Multi-variable Controller Design For Buck, Boost Based Double-Input DC-DC Converter
abstract: In this paper, a quantitative feedback theory (QFT) based robust controller is designed for double-input DC-DC converter. Relative gain array (RGA) based interaction analysis is used for determining the controlling inputs and controlled outputs pairing. A charge-pump based double-input DC-DC converter is used as an example to explain the QFT robust diagonal controller design methodology. Performance specifications are enforced to handle the parametric uncertainties. For stable and reliable power management, two control-loops are adopted. One for current control and another for load voltage regulation. A 60/24 V to 48 V, 100 W 50 kHz double-input converter system is considered to demonstrate the QFT based multi-variable controller design. Effectiveness of diagonal controller pair is investigated through simulations and found that the results are in close agreement with analytical studies.

articleTitle: A Modified Dual Switch High Gain Boost Converter: Design and Analysis
abstract: This study introduces a dual-switch non-isolated boost converter (DSNIBC) which increases the voltage gain without operating non-isolated boost converter (NIBC) at high-duty ratios by adding a diode-switch pair and switched Inductor to NIBC. The insertion of an additional switch also rise the Liberty of Control (LoC) for both inductor current and output voltage simultaneously using control variables d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, in comparison to NIBC. A capacitor is also connected across the load to reduce the ripples. The proposed converter with continuous input current and low ripple is well-suited for renewable energy applications due to its ability to respond quickly to changes in input conditions. The characteristics of DSNIBC are supported by simulations and developed by mathematical derivations. For example, according to the simulation results, voltage gains rise from 5.67 to 15 when the duty ratio of the additional switch in DSNIBC goes from 0 to 0.1.

articleTitle: Phase Shifting Techniques Implementation in DAB Converter for EV Applications
abstract: The effective power conversion technologies are required for best performance of electric vehicles. The implementation of different phase-shifting techniques in a DAB converter, which are feasible solution for EVs due to its highly efficient and its bidirectional power flow capabilities. In this context the operating principle of Dual Active Bridge Converter, equations, and performance using simulations are interpreted. The findings show significant inferences in efficiency and other different parameters, highlighting the potential of phase-shifting approaches in enhancing EV systems.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Planning of Renewables to Optimize Hosting Capacity and Voltage Deviation Index in Distribution System with Electric Vehicles
abstract: Increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) in distribution system makes it imperative to evaluate the hosting capacity (HC) of distribution system. HC is defined as the maximum amount of distributed generation (DG) that a distribution system can accommodate without effecting its reliability and voltage quality. To this end, a multi-objective stochastic framework for enhancing penetration of wind-based and solar photovoltaic DG in distribution system is presented. Further, distribution system is considered to be integrated with controllable electric vehicles (EVs). The proposed multi-objective framework considers two conflicting objectives namely maximizing HC and minimizing voltage deviation index (VDI). The weighted sum method is used to solve multi-objective formulation. The efficacy of proposed model is validated on real-life 108 Indian distribution system with different penetration of EVs. Simulation results highlight the competence of mul-objective formulation to evaluate HC.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Renewable Energy Integration on the Grid: A Case Study of Ghana
abstract: Grid integration of Renewable energy sources (RES) is gaining significant traction due to their capacity to produce electricity at a lower cost and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions like CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, and NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>. However, the unpredictability and variability of these generation sources pose challenges to grid operators in maintaining the generation demand balance. This necessitates an adequate balancing capacity from traditional sources to maintain grid reliability and security. In this context, the given study proposed a production cost simulation using the Multi Area Production Cost Simulation software of General Electric (MAPS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>) to analyze the impact of RES. The country level grid of Ghana is considered for the purpose of study and analysis for the years 2018 and 2030. The simulation is carried out based on anticipated generation capacity mix, load projections, and renewable generation profiles to evaluate the variation in total cost of generation, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, fuel consumed, and average spot price.

articleTitle: GWO Assisted Load Frequency Control of Power System Considering Electric Vehicle
abstract: Nowadays, power system is modernized, i.e., renewable energy sources are increasing rapidly, making the architecture more fragile. Therefore, operating within the allowable range requires effective optimization techniques, controllers, and demand-side participation. Strengthening the system responsiveness is one of the benefits of using load frequency control (LFC) based on standard controllers. But this makes the system more difficult and time-consuming. This study uses the grey wolf optimization (GWO) to apply on standard PID(proportional integral derivative) controller for LFC issue in an isolated power system with demand-side participation of electric vehicles (EVs), which involves vehicle to the grid (V2G) technology. A thought for connecting vehicles to the grid is that an electric-powered vehicle battery can improve the frequency deviation. Thus, the amount of battery capacity needed can be decreased by the deployment of these vehicles. The GWO algorithm optimizes the parameters of traditional PID controller using integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) as an objective function. A comparative analysis is performed using other algorithm to show the robustness of the schemed GWO algorithm. The simulation outcomes show that the proposed work equipped with these vehicles has better overshooting, undershooting, and settling time capability and suppresses system frequency fluctuations effectively.

articleTitle: Detection of IGBT Bond-Wire Lift-off Using Acoustic Pressure Scattering
abstract: This paper investigates the detection of damaged bond wires in Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) modules through the application of acoustic pressure scattering techniques. IGBTs are critical components utilized in systems such as renewable energy installations and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems. Within these modules, bond wires serve to connect the semiconductor die to external terminals while providing structural support. However, these wires are susceptible to cracking or detachment under high-stress conditions induced by heavy electrical currents and temperature fluctuations, leading to potential module failures. The proposed study employs COMSOL Multiphysics to examine the effectiveness of sound waves and acoustic pressure scattering in detecting these compromised bond wires. A detailed IGBT model was constructed, incorporating 16 bond wires, and subjected to various defect scenarios at two distinct frequencies: 5 MHz, and 30 MHz. The scenarios included a module with no defects, a single defective wire, five defective wires, and ten defective wires. Comprehensive acoustic scattering analyses were conducted, capturing the pressure amplitudes around the bond wires in a two-dimensional format. The objective of these analyses is to evaluate the influence of different defect severities on the acoustic signatures and to identify the optimal frequency for accurate defect detection. It was observed that the 5 MHz frequency provides more distinct insights into the quantity of defects when compared to the 30 MHz frequency.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Off-Board Smart Bidirectional EV Charger for Peak Load Levelling
abstract: A huge adoption of Electric Vehicles necessitates advanced integration techniques with the electric grid to ensure grids’ efficiency. This paper focuses on a three-phase smart off-board bidirectional charger for Battery Electric Vehicles, capable of a seamless transition between Grid-to-Vehicle and Vehicle-to-Grid operations. The charger equipped with an innovative automatic switching mechanism is a significant feature that enables peak load levelling without compromising grid integrity. An LCL filter is incorporated to maintain high-quality sinusoidal grid currents. The design further ensures battery longevity and performance by integrating safeguards against overcharging and over-discharging. Crucially, this system empowers users by allowing them to select their preferred operational mode, independent of the battery’s State of Charge, thus offering unparalleled flexibility in energy management. This research advances EV infrastructure development, providing a scalable and user-centric solution that accommodates both individual and grid-wide energy demands.

articleTitle: Grid Integrated PV Based EV Charging Station
abstract: This paper presents a new control approach for a three-phase, grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) array and battery energy storage system (BESS) interface for an electric vehicle (EV) charging station. During daytime, the PV array and BESS charge the EV, while the grid supplies power if PV output is unavailable. The model’s primary goal is to stabilize grid active power under all conditions. The battery’s charging and discharging functions balance power to meet EV demand. The voltage source converter (VSC) serves as an active power filter, reducing harmonics on the AC side. The control system is responsive, adaptable, and operates smoothly under varying conditions such as PV or BES disconnection and constant grid power mode.

Author Keywords: Second-Order Generalized Integrator - Quadrature Signal Generator (SOGI-QSG)

articleTitle: Design of Fuzzy controller for tracking of desired trajectory of 2-DOF Aero System
abstract: This paper presents a unique design of fuzzy controller, used for attitude control of a two Degrees of freedom Aero flight control simulator. The proposed controller utilizes a parallel structure of Mamdani fuzzy system to track the attitude and overcome parametric uncertainties due to coupled dynamics of the system. To validate the proposed design, numerical simulations are carried out and been compared with existing methods. The tracking responses of yaw and pitch point out fast convergence of error with minimum overshoot in the presence of unmatched uncertainties.

articleTitle: CC-CV Charging of Lithium-ion Battery for Electric Vehicle Applications
abstract: In the realm of electric vehicles (EVs), efficient and reliable charging methods are fundamental to advancing the widespread adoption and sustainability of electric transportation. Among the various charging techniques, constant current constant voltage (CC-CV) charging has emerged as a prominent method for replenishing energy in lithium-ion batteries, the backbone of EV propulsion systems. CC-CV charging combines the benefits of both constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) charging phases to deliver a controlled and optimized charging process. During the CC phase, a constant charging current is supplied to the battery, ensuring a steady flow of electrical energy. As the battery approaches full capacity, the charging process transitions to the CV phase, where the charging voltage is held constant to prevent overcharging. This dual-phase charging strategy offers several advantages, including faster charging times, improved energy efficiency, and enhanced battery lifespan. This paper explores the principles, modelling, and MATLAB simulation of CCCV charging for lithium-ion battery.

articleTitle: PV-fed Flyback-type Single-stage Single-phase Grid-tied System
abstract: This paper presents a design and control of a PV-fed flyback-type single-stage single-phase grid-tied system (PVFSSGS). This single-stage topology reduces the system complexity, provides electrical isolation among PV panels and the grid, and mitigates the circulation of leakage current. The PVFSSGS’s control ensures the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and delivers the power to the grid in a synchronized fashion. The MPPT operation is achieved by using a novel reduced-rule fuzzy logic control. To ensure the control in real-time, it is implemented on controller TMS320F28379D, and real-time signals are sensed using a low-cost isolation amplifier (HCPL-7840) based signal condition circuits.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Power Output Predictions: Analyzing ARIMA and S-ARIMA Models for Short-Term Forecasting
abstract: As the world evolves towards sustainable energy, solar photovoltaic energy has become an important technology in the transition to renewable energy. Solar photovoltaic systems provide clean and more abundant energy by converting sunlight directly into electricity. However, interoperability of solar energy generation poses serious problems in terms of grid security and power management due to climate change, time of day and seasonal changes. Accurately predicting short-term solar photovoltaic energy generation is critical to ensuring efficient power distribution, reducing operating costs and ensuring product reliability in electricity usage. Therefore, statistics and machine learning have become important in solving these prediction problems.This paper explores the effectiveness of ARIMA (AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average) and SARIMA (Seasonal AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average) models in short-term hourly forecasting of solar PV power. The study evaluates the models’ performance in predicting hourly data, emphasizing its applicability to weather prediction, energy consumption and financial markets. Comparative analysis is conducted to highlight the strengths and limitations of each model.

articleTitle: Assessment of Bus Voltage Variations in the Distribution Network using PDF Estimators
abstract: The bus voltage regulation in the distribution network limits the active power injection from connected PV system, mainly with high solar radiation. The voltage improvement via reactive power (PV inverter) in turn depends on its hosting capacity. In this study, different probability density function (PDF) estimators; Gaussian function, LCV-KDE, Gaussian kernel (MATLAB function) and B-spline are used in analysis for distribution of voltage at the buses in the network. It is shown that normal distributed Gaussian function fails to correctly estimate the voltage profile distribution. On other hand, B-spline based estimator is capable to indicate local peaks of PDF, which can be helpful to correlate the voltage variations at different buses.

articleTitle: Medium Voltage Grid Connected MMC Operation with Reduced Sensors and Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis Feature
abstract: Recent research has focused on minimizing the number of sensors to reduce hardware complexity in Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC). While normal MMC operation with fewer sensors has shown reasonable performance, diagnosing switch or diode fault remains a challenge.
