Limited studies have addressed fault diagnosis in MMCs with reduced sensor operation, but these often suffer from either complex fault diagnosis methods or dependency on additional measurements. This work introduces a novel approach for diagnosing both switch and diode open circuit faults by leveraging existing measurements such as arm voltages, observed arm currents, and switching status, thereby eliminating the need for additional sensors. The proposed fault diagnosis method also avoids the use of a computationally intensive software approach. The simulation and experimental outcomes of a grid connected MMC validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in diagnosing switch and diode open circuit fault.

Author Keywords: switch and diode open circuit fault diagnosis

articleTitle: Design & Implementation of Cuk Converter Based Bridgeless Rectifier
abstract: An optimum and efficient configuration for effective AC-DC power conversion is bridgeless cuk converter operating in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) due to its unique ability to automatically shape the input current. This paper discusses the theoretical analysis and implementation aspects of bridgeless ćuk converter. The converter is modelled using Current Injected Equivalent Circuit Approach (CIECA) to obtain transfer function and suitable compensator is designed. The control strategy is designed and realized using a low cost dsPIC33FJ12MC202 microcontroller. A cost effective method to sense the output voltage is also proposed. The results are verified and tested on 80V, 100W laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of SEIG coupled Micro-Hydro and PV-BSS-based remote Microgrid
abstract: This paper presents an extensive study on the application of model predictive control (MPC) for enhancing the performance of a self-excited induction generator (SEIG)-based micro-hydro system integrated with a photovoltaic (PV) array and battery storage system (BSS) in a remote microgrid. The hybrid energy system aims to provide reliable and sustainable power to isolated regions with limited or unavailable grid access. The proposed MPC strategy actively manages the power distribution between the micro-hydro generator, PV array, and battery storage system (BSS), ensuring voltage and frequency regulation of the microgrid. A power quality enhancement feature has also been incorporated in the developed MPC to mitigate the current harmonics generated by nonlinear loads and maintain better voltage at the point of common coupling (PCC). A laboratory prototype of the microgrid is developed and tested for various loads and operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed MPC approach in maintaining stable microgrid voltage and frequency even under fluctuating load demands and PV power generation.

articleTitle: Impact Assessment of Distributed Storage in Active Distribution Networks using Current Sensitivity-based OPF
abstract: Integration of distributed storage (DS) offers a significant potential for managing the variability and unpredictability of renewable energy sources (RES) in active distribution networks (ADNs). In this regard, this paper explores the dynamic capabilities of DS by leveraging current sensitivity (CS)-based OPF on radial and weakly meshed ADNs. This work employs a network sensitivity-based OPF for effective integration and management of DS. Results demonstrate that DS integration improves voltage profiles and enhances load balancing. In weakly meshed ADNs, economic benefits are observed through cost savings from decreased energy losses and nodal distribution locational marginal prices (DLMPs). This highlights the critical role of DS in optimizing power flows, offering valuable insights for the distribution network operator (DNO) to enhance ADN techno-economic viability.

articleTitle: Predicting Cascading Failures in Power Systems using Machine Learning
abstract: Cascading failure studies help assess and enhance the robustness of power systems against severe power outages. Onset time is a critical parameter in the analysis and management of power system stability and reliability, representing the timeframe within which initial disturbances may lead to subsequent cascading failures. In this paper, different traditional machine learning algorithms are used to predict the onset time of cascading failures. The prediction task is articulated as a multi-class classification problem, employing machine learning algorithms. The results on the UIUC 150-Bus power system data available publicly show high classification accuracy with Random Forest. The hyperparameters of the Random Forest classifier are tuned using Bayesian Optimization. This study highlights the potential of machine learning models in predicting cascading failures, providing a foundation for the development of more resilient power systems.

articleTitle: Power quality analysis of three stage fifteen level cascaded multilevel inverter by using FPGA controller for EV application
abstract: Sustainable power generation is characterized by zero carbon emissions in specific circumstances. However, this is primarily owing to their inherent generating mode, which involves the use of direct current (DC) power, as seen in solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, fuel cells, and other similar technologies. It is intended to encourage inverters to provide electricity to alternate current (AC) loads. Ensuring power quality is crucial while performing DC/AC inversion and is also vital for major electric vehicle (EV) applications, such as powering the EV motor. The required inverters can be the typical three-stage fifteen-level cascaded multilevel inverter. Enhancing the reliability of renewable energy sources can be achieved by employing EV motors and developing a 3-stage, 15-level inverter. This approach improves performance by lowering the number of switches and minimizing total harmonic distortion (THD). The utilization of pulse width modulation technology, in conjunction with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) algorithm, results in a reduction in the number of switches and facilitates the identification of faults through diagnostic processes. The recommended controller employs an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to precisely categorize errors in the proposed Multi-Level Inverter (MLI). In addition, the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) is evaluated for various load conditions. The datasets are acquired by MATLAB simulation. The datasets are used for training and testing to identify the most optimal Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique.

articleTitle: A High Speed Half-Bridge Gate Driver Circuit Design Using Discrete Electronic Components
abstract: This paper details the design, simulation, and validation of a high-frequency half-bridge gate driver circuit, based on a bootstrap circuit, using readily available components. Capable of switching frequencies up to 200 kHz, the gate driver features programmable dead time and a shutdown input to enhance modularity and practicality. Its real-life applicability was demonstrated through hardware testing with a synchronous buck converter, proving its effectiveness in practical applications.

articleTitle: Transformerless Inverter with Dynamic Voltage Boost and Zero leakage Current for PV System
abstract: Transformerless inverters (TIs) are highly efficient and have a high power density, making them a popular choice for grid-connected solar PV applications. This paper introduces a novel common-ground transformerless step-up 5level inverter design utilizing a single DC voltage source devoid of leakage current suitable for grid-connected PV applications. The proposed inverter is based on a hybrid switched capacitor (SC) concept, which uses integration of the boost inductor to facilitate continuous input current and dynamic voltage gain. The proposed circuit comprises eight switches and two SCs powered by a single input DC source. The primary advantages of the proposed single-stage topology encompass its commonground nature, boosting capability, reduced component count, lower cost, and smaller size compared to recently developed five-level topologies. However, these inverters commonly encounter issues with leakage current, which can lead to power losses and safety concerns. The proposed inverter design addresses this concern effectively. The configuration of the proposed inverter demonstrates a shared ground connection between the input and output terminals, ensuring a constant total common mode voltage (CMV). A thorough mathematical analysis of the proposed inverter was conducted, accompanied by the MATLAB/Simulink simulation results presentation. The simulation outcomes highlight the inverter's ability to boost output voltage, eliminate leakage current, and maintain suitable total harmonic distortion levels in output voltage and current waveforms.

articleTitle: Investigating PV Power Loss Correlations with Environmental Factors: A Case Study from Delhi
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems exhibit a high degree of environmental sensitivity, which can result in power losses and reduced system efficiency. To analyze power loss in PV systems, this paper presents an analytical method that uses the Random Forest algorithm while accounting for environmental factors like dust density, temperature, irradiance, humidity, and wind speed. To investigate these relationships, cross-sectional data were analyzed. The data came from rooftop PV plant situated at a University in Delhi, India, were collected between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2021. Because of its ability to manage non-linear relationships between variables and enable a thorough understanding of complex interactions, the Random Forest model was chosen. It can be helpful in predicting power outages as well as identifying how specific environmental factors affected the operation of the system. Pair plots and scatter plots were used in data preprocessing and exploratory analysis to show that dust concentration is one of the main factors affecting power loss. Dust concentration is closely correlated with ambient temperature, highlighting the urgent need for strategies to mitigate these impacts to increase the efficiency of PV systems. The data reveals that power loss peaks around 2000 W, indicating a significant loss threshold. The results highlight the need for ongoing observation and flexible management to improve performance in a variety of environmental settings.

articleTitle: Error Minimization based Stability Preserved Order Abatement Framework for Linear Systems
abstract: In this article, a new Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA) has been proposed for Order Abatement (OA) of the High Order System (HOS). Integral Square Error (ISE) has been utilized as an Objective Function for OA to minimize the error between the HOS and Proposed Abated System (AS) to find its unknown coefficients. Two HOS have been tested as an example of the Proposed HBA to demonstrate the efficiency of the Proposed HBA. For OA comparison of HOS and Proposed AS with other recently published AS have been considered in both examples. Various Performance Indices and Time Response parameters are compared by Proposed AS with recently published AS in the literature and these are represented in tabular form. It can be observed from the tested HOS that the Proposed HBA always provides stable AS if the Original/ HOS is stable.

articleTitle: Variable Step-size LMS Filter for Power Quality Enhancement using Grid Supportive Photovoltaic System
abstract: The emergence of semiconductor technology and applications related to switching devices have caused many problems related to power quality (PQ) such as harmonics, voltage fluctuations and power oscillations. In order to overcome these issues, inverter is connected at distribution end alongside photovoltaic source at DC-bus to enhance the PQ and active power submission to utility grid. The accuracy and performance of grid connected PV systems are depending on performance of control structure. This paper presents, an adaptive algorithm based on variable step size least mean square (VSS-LMS) has been proposed for controlling the distributed static compensator (DSTATCOM). In this structure a new parameter according to the error-based autocorrelation function has been introduced to vary the step size for weight updating process. This adjustment not only maintains the immunity against the external disturbances but also controls the misadjustment and convergence time independently. In the overall control structure, the independent weight of the three phases distorted current have been estimated for further generation of reference current signals. The proposed control methodology is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and tested using real-time simulator. The simulation results under various practical scenarios such as unbalanced loading, sudden loading, harmonic penetration etc. presents the superior performance of proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Different Reactive Power Conditions in DAB
abstract: Dual active bridge (DAB) converters have drawn attention due to the advantages of bidirectional power flow and galvanic isolation. Reactive power is better controlled in dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation over single phase-shift (SPS) modulation due to the presence of two-degree freedom of power flow. In the existing literature, analysis of reactive power is not performed for all combinations of phase-shift ratios in DPS of the DAB converter. The existing expressions of reactive power are not applicable for several cases. Therefore, the paper analyses the reactive power present in DPS of the DAB converter for all combinations of internal and external phase-shift ratios. The derived expression of reactive power in each case is different from other cases. All the theoretical expressions are verified with MATLAB simulations and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Real Time Simulation for Testing a Variable Speed Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Plant Connected to an EHV Transmission Network using RTDS
abstract: India’s commitment to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, is to reduce the carbon footprint by 45% and energy requirement from non-fossil fuel sources by 50% by 2030. This energy transition incorporates intermittent sources like solar and wind having low inertia and fast control characteristic of the converters. This poses grid stability issues caused by rapid frequency collapse during faults and islanding. Energy storage systems enable the reliable operation and integration of renewable energy sources in power grid by providing frequency control and load leveling services to power grids with high penetration of renewables. Pumped hydro storage can balance short-term intermittent generation by providing fast power ramps, as well as provide long-term load-leveling during seasonal weather patterns. In this study, a variable-speed pumped storage machine is taken as the test case. Large head variation makes these projects even more challenging, and hence, the effect of grid conditions on the machines were thoroughly studied for the reliable and efficient operation of the pumped storage plant. Conventional modeling of the hydro turbines is followed for the turbine mode of application, and for the pumping mode simulation, the system implemented the pump head-flow curve with gating effects that provides additional friction to the system. Furthermore, the modeling is carried out using the Real Time Digital Power System Simulator to realize the real-time response of the machine towards the transients occurring in the system.

Author Keywords: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in Active Distribution Network using Voltage and Current Features
abstract: This paper presents a fault detection and classification method in an active distribution network using relay voltage and current signals. The features are obtained using the empirical wavelet transform as well as other statistical indices, which are utilized to develop the machine learning-based protection models. Further, principal component analysis is deployed for the purpose of feature dimensionality reduction. The IEEE 13-bus network integrated with inverter-based distributed generation units modelled in PSCAD/EMTDC is considered in the study. A large data set comprising of diverse fault and non-fault events is obtained from the simulated network to obtain the protection models. Performances of the selected relays in the network are demonstrated regarding fault detection and faulty phase identification. The results exhibit robust and reliable response to the network events and demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed work particularly with regard to the uncertainty in the network operation scenarios. Moreover, the intelligent models can be implemented in the protection system along with the available protection schemes.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network-Based State-of-Charge Estimation of Li-ion Batteries for Electrified Transportation
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) battery management system (BMS) depends heavily on the accurate state of charge (SoC) statistic. It impacts the lifespan, effectiveness, and credibility of the Li-ion battery (LIB). However, erratic battery dynamics and SOC fluctuations imposed by external variables like ambient temperature, battery age, and number of charge/discharge cycles make precise SoC estimation difficult. Consequently, using cutting-edge techniques is crucial for accurate SoC estimation. Deep learning models' computational intelligence and self-learning abilities have proven them beneficial for SoC estimation. This paper presents a deep neural network (DNN) based SoC estimator design approach. The model is trained and validated using the Unified Driving Schedule (LA92) drive cycle, and a comprehensive analysis has been carried out at different temperatures. Finally, the model's accuracy is calculated using various error metrics, and the results indicate that the model succeeds in achieving 0.58%, 0.69%, and 0.6% mean absolute error (MAE) at 0°C, 25°C, and 40°C respectively.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration of PV Array Based on Index Sum (IS) Method to Improve Power Generation under Partial Shading Condition
abstract: Abstract Partial shading in Photovoltaic arrays reduces power generation, causes multiple peaks in P-V characteristics, and failure of conventional MPP trackers. This paper proposes a static reconfiguration technique to enhance the power output under partial shading conditions by arranging modules in a Total Cross Tied (TCT) connected PV array using the Index Sum (IS) method. This arrangement uses a column-wise rearrangement procedure to disperse the shading effects over an array to achieve uniform row current without altering the electrical connection. The study investigates the performance of a 6 × 6 array using MATLAB under four different shading patterns and compares the method with standard TCT in terms of percentage power enhancement (%PE). Results show that using the IS method for module arrangement enhances output power ranging from 7.87% to 20.2% compared to the TCT configuration, and minimizes the multiple power peaks from the PV characteristics under partially shaded conditions.

articleTitle: Efficiency Based Control Strategy for Off-Grid PV integrated Battery Storage System
abstract: Energy storage is necessary in off-grid photovoltaic (PV) systems, which require a battery charge controller. However, because of the unpredictable weather patterns and the constant changes in energy demand, the delivery of PV power to the load may fluctuate, resulting in a decrease in battery charging efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an enhanced power balance control strategy that focuses on optimizing battery efficiency by taking into account the state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH). This strategy ensures a balanced distribution of PV power between the DC load and the battery, maximizing the utilization of solar energy while effectively charging the battery. As batteries age, their internal resistance increases and their capacity decreases. This means that battery storage systems (BSS) need an algorithm to effectively manage the battery's state when used with renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Development of a Fuzzy-PI tuned Bidirectional Charger for Electric Three-Wheeler Applications
abstract: The growing worldwide market for electric vehicles (EVs) has put pressure on automotive system developers to improve charging efficiency and enhance the charging infrastructure. Bidirectional chargers support the grid by flowing the power in the two directions, i.e. functioning in both V2G and G2V modes. In this paper, a bidirectional converter interfaces a fixed DC bus that supports EV battery charging and discharging operation, is presented and simulated in a MATLAB environment. A Fuzzy Logic tuned Proportional Integral (FLPI) is designed using MATLAB Simulink to enhance the charger's performance. This paper also presents a performance comparative analysis of the FLPI and conventionally used PI Controller, highlighting the FLPI controller's advantages. FLPI is better than the conventional PI because of low errors, faster response time, better transient performance and improved robustness. The charger is developed and simulated for a 600V DC supply with a peak output power of 10kW. The simulation results demonstrate the charging and discharging of a 72V 150 Ah Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery for electric-3-wheeler applications.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Noise Modelling and Analysis of a High-gain Quadratic Boost DC-DC Converter
abstract: The Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of Power converters has gained huge attention with the increase in utilization of high-frequency switching converters. High-frequency switching of the device causes high dv/dt, leading to the formation of parasitic capacitances between the switching node and the ground, which in turn introduces common-mode current. The PCB track inductances and resistances of the converter also cause resonant peaks in the noise spectrum and need to be evaluated for prediction of the conducted EMI spectrum of a converter. This paper analyzes the common-mode noise of a high-gain quadratic converter by developing the Common-Mode equivalent circuit and studying the effect of the individual noise sources. The parasitic parameters of the converter’s PCB are derived using ANSYS Q3D while the EMI simulation is conducted in PSIM.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Compact and Robust SiC MOSFET Based Converter for EV Application
abstract: The electrification of transport sector brings the revolution in the field of converter design for battery charging and traction. The key performance indicators for converters like high power density, efficiency, lower cost, compact in size etc. are considered during the designing of converter. The Wide Bandgap (WBG) devices like SiC and GaN helps to achieve efficient and high power density in the field of converter design. And also, they operates at a very high frequency. The voltage and current rating of WBG are high in comparison to conventional Si switches. This paper presents unique design methodology of a 3kW SiC MOSFET based three-phase converter suitable for AC-DC, DC-AC power conversion and electric vehicle (EV) applications. This paper presents the designed sensors for DC-link voltage, AC voltage and current, which makes the converter suitable for any close loop operation, PFC or DC-AC power conversion. This paper explains the design steps and selection of parameters for SiC MOSFET based converter. The Simulation and hardware results are presented to validate the design of converter.

articleTitle: Advanced Fault Identification, Classification, and Localization Technique for Enhanced Protection in DC Zonal Microgrids
abstract: This paper presents an efficient protection technique in DC zonal microgrids. Localization of faults in DC microgrids presents significant challenges because of the DC network’s inherent low-impedance properties. The proposed method operates by utilizing the current, voltage, and line parameters under fault conditions. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated on a 600 V DC zonal microgrid in the MATLAB (Simulink) software, successfully identifying both pole-to-pole and pole-to-ground fault types across a broad range of fault resistances and locations. The simulation outcomes validate the efficacy of the suggested method in accurately identifying, classifying, and localization of faults under varying fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Intelligent Frequency Control Mechanism of Renewable Shared Interconnected Power System with Communication Delay
abstract: This paper introduces a fuzzy logic-based intelligent frequency control approach for renewable-dominated time-delayed interconnected power systems (IPS). A two-area IPS model including solar, wind, thermal and gas power generators with hydrogen-based energy storage systems is designed. A time delay (TD) of 2 seconds is considered in both areas as well as all the physical constraints and nonlinearities like valve limit, dead bands and rate constraints are also considered in the designing of the plant. A fuzzy logic-driven proportional derivative plus integral (F-PD+I) controller is designed for the load frequency control (LFC) of considered IPS. To select the optimal solution for the proposed F-PD+I controller, a physics-inspired optimization called gradient-based optimizer (GBO) is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is tested over random load variations and the results reveal the superior performance of the F-PD+I controller over PI and PID controllers.

articleTitle: A Robust Deep Learning Framework for Anomaly Detection in Smart Grid
abstract: Identification of irregularities is a major and common problem that costs utility companies a lot of money and energy worldwide. The attack surface has definitely increased with the deployment of smart meters and other modern metering infrastructures. To combat such attacks, this study presents a robust deep learning framework designed for the identification of both cyber and physical anomalies within the power grid. Utilizing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, the frame-work aims to discern underlying patterns in energy consumption. To assess its effectiveness, a comparative analysis was conducted, evaluating the performance of the proposed LSTM model against established machine learning models such as Random Forest (RF), K-nearest neighbor (Knn), XGBoost, Decision Tree (DT), and Naive Bayes (NB). To address data imbalance, six distinct synthetic attacks were generated. Additionally, 5-fold cross-validation was employed to enhance the reliability and generalization of the model evaluation process.

articleTitle: Tracking Global Peak Under Mismatching Conditions With Reduced Steady-State Oscillation For PV Module
abstract: A modified perturbation based algorithm to track the global peak (GP) with reduced steady-state oscillation for a photovoltaic (PV) module under mismatching conditions is proposed in this work. The global peak tracking algorithm begins by initializing datasheet parameters of the PV module. The zone is decided based on the range of PV voltage. A perturbation-based technique is used to identify the closest peak. The location of the operating point will be shifted to different zones where there is a possibility of occurrence of GP. The highest value of power among all the peaks is considered as global peak and a conventional perturbation based method is utilized to accurately achieve the global peak. A new methodology is implemented in this paper to nullify the oscillation in the value of duty ratio once the global peak is achieved. This leads to significant reduction of oscillation in the values of PV voltage. The setup containing boost converter connected between PV module and load is used for implementing the proposed method. Further, a comparison is made with the recently published research paper on global peak tracking and a perturbation based method at different shading patterns.

articleTitle: Pareto Optimality Based Zonal Allocation of Distributed Energy Resources Considering Technical and Economic Constraints
abstract: Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) play a crucial role in enhancing the resilience of distribution networks during High-Impact Low-Frequency (HILF) events. Optimal allocation of DERs is essential to minimize capital costs while improving the operational performance of the distribution network. This paper introduces a Pareto Optimality Based Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) approach for the strategic placement of DERs across various zones of a distribution network. We formulate a multi-objective optimization problem within the fuzzy domain, aiming to minimize DER installation costs, reduce power losses and enhance the voltage profile of the network. The proposed optimization algorithm is evaluated using the IEEE 123-bus test system through a co-simulation between MATLAB and OpenDSS. The results illustrate that the proposed approach effectively balances cost and power losses while ensuring the voltage profile remains within the NERC standards.

articleTitle: IoT Based Intelligent Solar Tracking System for Smart Energy Application
abstract: The global demand for electrical energy continues to grow, and solar energy has emerged as one of the most efficient and sustainable methods of electricity generation. Traditional power production, heavily reliant on natural resources like coal, faces increasing challenges due to resource depletion. To address these concerns and enhance efficiency, solar tracking systems have been developed. Solar energy, harnessed from the sun, is a renewable resource, making it a crucial component of future energy solutions. In this paper, we explore the design and implementation of an IoT-based solar tracking system. The proposed model enables the solar tracker to monitor the sun’s position and adjust its alignment to minimize the angle of incidence of incoming sunlight, thereby maximizing energy capture. The system is developed using light sensors, Arduino IDE, Arduino UNO, and a DC motor. It is mounted on a rooftop with an unobstructed view of sunlight, and the panel’s mobility is observed throughout the day. The generated power is utilized for various applications, including street lamps and emergency lighting systems.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Cascaded H-Bridge based Enhanced-STATCOM in a Power Electronics Dominated Grid
abstract: Providing inertial power support from cascaded H-bridge (CHB)-based static synchronous compensators (STAT-COMs) significantly minimizes grid frequency deviation in a high-power electronics-based resources (PEBRs) network. However, power device faults in STATCOMS lead to frequency instability due to loss of energy. This study presents a novel approach to enhance the grid frequency characteristics even with multiple multi-phase device faults in CHB-STATCOM. This paper proposes an enhanced CHB-STATCOM (E-STATCOM) topology that aims to achieve balanced line voltages during switch faults and effectively handle large-frequency events. In this topology, a three-phase, battery-operated voltage source inverter (BOVSI) is connected in series with a three-phase CHB STATCOM. During post-fault conditions, the modulating signals of the enhanced converter are adjusted to achieve balanced line voltages. The BOVSI is calibrated to maintain the pre-fault line voltage and provide sufficient inertial power support to minimise frequency deviation during various frequency events. However, providing inertial power by BOVSI needs to measure the rate of change of frequency deviation. Obtaining this term by directly differentiating the frequency change sensed from the phase-locked loop (PLL) generates noise. This study uses frequency-locked loops (FLL) to generate a time-derivative term of frequency change, considerably reducing noise.

articleTitle: LSTM-Driven State of Charge Estimation for Battery Management
abstract: This research presents a method for estimating the state of charge (SOC) of lithium-ion batteries using a neural network model. The primary challenges of this study include accurately capturing the nonlinear behavior of battery SOC under various driving conditions and temperatures. The approach involved initially cleaning the dataset and calculating the SOC values. The data is then scaled appropriately, and the neural network model was trained using diverse driving cycles and a combination of these cycles at various temperatures. The trained model was evaluated on both a single driving cycle and a mixed driving cycle, which integrated all driving conditions. The results demonstrate that the model achieves an R2 score of over 0.98 in SOC estimation, indicating its robustness and reliability across different scenarios. This high level of accuracy suggests that the neural network model worked well in real-life battery management systems, making accurate SOC predictions in a wide range of operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Shadow Detection in PV Module Using Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems are often affected by dust, dirt, and obstructions such as trees and buildings, leading to partial shading and uneven sunlight distribution. This results in significant energy losses and impacts the electrical performance of PV generators. Accurate shadow boundary extraction is crucial for inspecting and monitoring PV panels, as it helps define module boundaries clearly for developers and maintenance providers. This article introduces a novel method for extracting shadow boundaries in PV plants using a deep neural network designed for shadow detection. Leveraging a shading dataset, the approach incorporates a spatial attention module to enhance spatial info extraction from feature maps. This module effectively captures semantic details both horizontally and vertically, addressing challenges in identifying small or ambiguous shadow areas and minimizing missed or incorrectly detected shadows. The results validate that the trained model distinguish the borders of shaded PV module with an accuracy of 99.33 %.

articleTitle: Case Study: Adoption and Analysis of Electric Vehicle Policy
abstract: Making the transition to electric vehicles is one of the most crucial strategies for reducing urban air pollution and addres sing climate change (EVs). In order to encourage this shift, India has implemented government programs like the Faster Acceptance and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME) plans. This is because declining battery costs and advancements in technology are boosting global acceptance of these vehicles. The research looks at how different EV policy have affected the number of EV registrations in Jaipur, with a particular emphasis on 2,3, and 4wheelers.The analysis takes into account the quantity of newly registered electric vehicles as well as the penetration of electric vehicles among these total new registrations during various time periods in Jaipur. Registration data for vehicles was gathered, classified as EV or non-EV, and cross referenced with applicable EV policies. In order to analyze the impact of important policies on EV adoption in Jaipur, the paper highlights programs including the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP 2020), FAME India Scheme, and state government incentives for Rajasthan. Findings indicate a considerable increase in EV registrations, with noteworthy increases in EV penetration across all vehicle categories, especially during the execution of FAME Phase II and state level incentives. With the greatest impact shown in the two- and three-wheeler sectors, the results highlight the significance of supportive policies in advancing the adoption of EVs.

articleTitle: Design of buck boost converter using single switch and positive output voltage for electric vehicle applications
abstract: Quadratic boost converter plus a D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>LC structure merges to give a unprecedented topology of a buck boost converter is proposed in this article. The topology is benefited with the following features. A single switch with continuous input current and can deliver non-inverting output voltage to the load. Higher voltage gain combined with larger effectiveness index is obtained. The blocking voltage across the switch is low. Only less number of elements are used. All these combined makes the topology aspiring for fuel cell vehicle applications. In steady state converter is analyzed in continuous conduction mode (CCM). Simulation is done in MATLAB environment and verified against theoretical values. Suitability of the topology proposed is elaborated in detail for electric vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Four-Level Diode-Clamped Based Twenty-Four Pulse VSC for HVDC Converter Applications
abstract: This paper presents a 24-pulse voltage source converter (VSC) system for high voltage direct current (HVDC) application. The system utilizes four-level neutral point clamped (NPC4L) converters in conjunction with star-delta transformer configurations to achieve a 24-pulse operation, which significantly reduces harmonics distortion. Converters are modulated using fundamental frequency switching (FFS), ensuring efficient power conversion and grid integration. Performance of a 1000MW HVDC system is validated through simulations in MATLAB Simulink, demonstrating effective harmonics reduction, steady-state and dynamic operation, making it suitable for HVDC integration.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Grid Integrated Photovoltaic System using Active Current Separation Technique
abstract: The integration of solar photovoltaic array needs a robust and fast control structure for dynamic performance. In view of this, a new active current separation technique-based controller is designed for faster inverter response under one AC power cycle during sudden switching in nonlinear load and photovoltaic current. This controller has unique capability of active current component separation with the help of simple mathematical operators. Moreover, optimized gains parameters is refined the response of outer voltage control loop. The proposed control structure continuously provides the load demand and supports the existing grid by supplying the maximum amount of available solar power at DC-bus terminals. Furthermore, the proposed system is designed to maintain power qualities, such as current balancing, harmonic mitigation, minimization of reactive power, improvement of power factor. The efficacy of control structure is tested through MATLAB/Simulink for various operating scenarios and validated using real time simulator OPAL-RT(OP4510)

articleTitle: Stacked Ensemble Learning for accurate Fault Diagnosis in AC Microgrid Systems
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) are small-scale power systems that encourage the use of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and they may or may not be supported by the main grid. MG provides resilience and reliability by decentralizing power generation, offering high efficiency and modularity by strategically managing generation as well as distribution creating a sustainable energy future. Surrounded by the advantages MG holds several challenges of fault detection due to bi-directional power flow, dynamic behavior of different energy sources, and varying magnitudes of fault current in different operating scenarios. To overcome these challenges a sturdy methodology is required which can work effectively and efficiently steer through a dynamic environment where power generation, consumption, and grid topology undergo rapid change. The approached methodology involves a novel ensemble stacking approach that uses several base models that take input data, and the output data of the base models act as input to the final meta-classifier model, which in turn results to give the final output. This paper highlights the potentiality of the ensemble stacking method in MG fault analysis application which is tested and validated in IEEE 7 BUS Real Time System and offers insights for improving the accuracy and efficiency of traditional models.

articleTitle: Observer-based Cuk Converter Control Design and Analysis
abstract: An observer-based Cuk converter control, design, and analysis are discussed in this paper. This control strategy can yield better dynamic as well as robust performance. In this scheme, the observer estimates the internal states of the system. It computes the estimation error which is the difference of estimated output and actual output and uses this to adjust the estimates of internal states of the system. This observer-based scheme provides better disturbance rejection ability than PI, and PID by estimating disturbance effects on states and compensating it through state feedback. For comparison purposes, the PI and PID controllers are also simulated and analyzed. After that, a theoretical analysis is carried out. The simulations indicate that without using extra sensors better dynamic responses are achievable against parameter variations. Simulation results are in line with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Multilevel Converter based PV-STATCOM with Global Maximum Power Point Tracking at Low Voltage during Partial Shading
abstract: The conventional photovoltaic-converters are usually a 2-stage converter, consisting of a DC-DC stage for MPPT operation followed by a central inverter for grid or load side control. This configuration faces difficulty when Global Maximum Power Point (GMPP) is located at lower voltage due to partial shading. In this paper, a configuration with single-stage power conversion and multilevel voltage pattern is proposed which offers three advantages like (i) low overall losses, and hence, improved efficiency, (ii) no need of ac-side passive filters, and (iii) capability to operate at low-voltage maximum power point. A multilevel converter is used where PV panels are directly conneted to each submodule. This paper focuses on the over-modulation situation in the submodule(s) due to voltage dip in the corresponding DC bus during partial shading. An Auxiliary submodule fed from tertiary winding of power transformer is incorporated to address the issues at low voltage GMPP. A technique to control active and reactive power of individual submodules is developed. The proposed topology and the control method are validated through MATLAB/Simulink and the results show satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Induction Motor,Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor and Line Start Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor using Finite Element Analysis
abstract: In this paper, a detailed comparative study of three motors namely, induction motor (IM), permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) and line start permanent magnet synchronous motor (LSPMSM) is done in terms of performance, design and details. To study the various structural and performance behavior of the three machines in finite element analysis (FEA) is used. The finite element method-based simulation results and all the geometry design details are studied and presented. A comparison of different performance parameters of the three motors are reported here in this paper. It has been found that the results of LSPMSM shows better performance than the IM and PMSM.

Author Keywords: Line start Permanent magnet synchronous motor (LSPMSM)

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of MPPT Controllers for Boost Converter in Solar PV Systems: PO, Incremental Conductance, and ANN
abstract: In order to maximise the performance of solar PV systems combined with a boost converter, this Paper provides a comparative examination of several Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) approaches, namely Incremental Conductance, Perturb and Observe, and Artificial Neural Network. Extensive MATLAB simulations were conducted to evaluate the output voltage, settling time, and duty cycle of each method under varying input conditions. The results demonstrate that while all methods successfully achieve the desired output voltage of 390V, the ANN method outperforms the others by providing precise tracking with minimal oscillation and a faster settling time of 0.03 seconds. In contrast, the IC and P&O methods, despite achieving similar output voltages, exhibit oscillations and longer settling times. These results demonstrate how well using a boost converter in combination with ANN-based MPPT may improve the stability and efficiency of solar energy systems. The report offers insightful information about the development and application of renewable energy technology.

articleTitle: Voltage Actuated Islanding Recognition Method Using Stockwell Transform and Voltage Change Rate
abstract: This paper presents a voltage actuated islanding recognition method (VAIRM). VAIRM is formulated by hybrid combination of voltage change rate (VCR) and voltage features computed by processing the voltage signals using Stockwell transform (ST). VCR is computed by differentiating the root mean (RMS) value of voltage. Voltage signal is decomposed using ST to compute the ST median factor (STMF) and STMF change rate (STMFCR). A hybrid islanding recognition indicator (HIRI) is designed to recognize the islanding events considering an islanding recognition threshold (IRTH). Study is performed using an IEEE-13 node test power network (TPN). Proposed method is effective to recognize the islanding event in the presence of wind power generator (WPG), solar power generator (SPG) and both SPG and WPG. VAIRM is also effective to discriminate the operational events such as outage of wind generator, outage of solar generator, load switching on and off events from the islanding events. Performance of VAIRM is not affected by noise and performs better compared to Wavelet packet transform (WPT) and ensemble based method.

articleTitle: A Novel Quasi Z-Source DC-DC Converter with Continuous Input Current for Solar PV Applications
abstract: In contrast to traditional DC-DC converters, a novel quasi Z-source (NQZS) converter is proposed in this study, which provides higher voltage gain at a lower duty ratio and reduces the stress of voltage and current on all the elements. Since this proposed converter has one controlled switch, it is often known as a single-switch circuit. The common ground between the input and output of the proposed NQZS converter eliminates EMI issues and minimizes the impact of parasitic capacitance. As a result, the efficiency and performance of the NQZS converter are significantly enhanced. This paper discusses the operating principle, steady-state analysis, and MATLAB simulation of the NQZS converter. This paper also compares the NQZS converter with other existing converters of the same category.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cyclic Degradation of Li-ion batteries
abstract: Battery degradation causes several adverse effects including reduced driving range and increased charging time. This affects the scheduling of Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) after few cycles of the battery usage in the grid. In this paper, a battery degradation model is adopted and various factors contributing to degradation were analyzed. In this model the effect of starting SoC (State of Charge) is also considered for better accuracy. The Capacity fade of batteries in different type of vehicles (Car, Bus, Truck) and BESS of various capacities is studied for various factors. Also, the optimal factors to reduce the degradation is studied. The temperature of the battery plays a crucial role in degradation. Higher C-rates accelerates the degradation. In addition, the starting SoC when under 50% also reduces the battery life. Simulation of vehicle batteries under various factors shows that higher battery capacity vehicles (bus in this case) degrades in less number of cycles. This can significantly impact the scheduling of EVs. The adopted model is compared with a data-fitting model of the same type. Results shows that there is 1% difference in lower and 2% higher C-rates respectively.

articleTitle: Loss Optimization of The High Frequency Solid State Transformer
abstract: In this paper, in high frequency operation of the solid state Transformer made by the ferrite cores yields the hysteresis, eddy current loss, copper loss and leakage power loss as structure of clarity of loss modeling and simulation. Classical optimization method is proposed for optimal solution of the power transfer. Core loss is independent of load current but it depends on the magnetic property how to optimize both parameters as optimal solution of the high switching frequency solid- state Transformer materials in a paper

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing for Energy Storage Systems in Hybrid Models Using a Novel Algorithmic Approach
abstract: Opting renewable for the energy needs is a promising solution to mitigate climate change. Though weather driven renewables like wind and solar are highly potent to satisfy the global energy demand, their intermittent nature makes them unreliable to rely on them as standalone solutions, utilizing their complementary nature and storing excess energy in energy storage systems (ESS) allows renewable to compete with conventional generation systems. The major challenges of integrating renewable with ESS include the need for a robust control infrastructure to manage energy flow, high costs, and potential hazards without a proper management system. This paper proposes a novel strategy with an optimized battery size selection and a control algorithm to operate the hybrid renewable system more efficiently and cost-effectively.

articleTitle: Dynamic Economic Dispatch With Storage using ADMM
abstract: The dependency on conventional power plants increases carbon emissions and generation costs, contributing to global warming, also the consideration factor for energy solving by centralised system for single point failure and flexibility. The article consider Distributed solution for the Dynamic Economic Dispatch Problem within island microgrids, considering total cost function, ramp limits and battery constraints. The integration of battery charging and discharging to balance system demand and generation and incorporating ramp limits for practicality, proposing a dynamic economic dispatch with storage approach that uses a distributed algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers. This algorithm effectively addresses battery constraints, generator capacity limits, and ramp rate constraints, offering a comprehensive solution for dynamic economic dispatch in microgrids operating in islanded modes. The results demonstrate the reduced variable costs for generators, peak savings, decreased carbon emissions, enhanced ancillary services, and improved intermittency mitigation.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electric Load Forecasting with Weather and Economic indicators using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Electric load forecasting is crucial for efficient energy management.This paper proposes a robust time-series forecasting system that predicts the daily electricity demand using additional features such as the 10-year break-even inflation, weather, unemployment rate and holidays. Among the machine learning models evaluated, CatBoost demonstrated the best performance due to its ability to effectively capture both general trends and seasonal patterns. This work highlights the idea of incorporating economic indicators to improve electricity demand forecasting.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-based Fractional Order Control for Effective Frequency Regulation
abstract: The objective of the presented work is to investigate the application of a fuzzy fractional order PID (fuzzy FOPID) controller in a two-area tied hybrid power system. This consists of integrating thermoelectric power plants that have been heated again, together with unpredictable renewable energy sources, inside a single control region. Additionally, there are hydropower plants in another control area. Renewable energy sources encompass wind power, solar thermal energy, and fuel cells. To simulate a realistic situation, the thermal and hydro systems are equipped with a generation rate constraint (GRC) and a governor dead band (GDB). Furthermore, the turbine incorporates boiler dynamics (BD), and both control regions experience a stochastic variation in load. Extensive simulations have shown that the Fuzzy FOPID control structure has superior performance compared to FOPID and PID controllers, as measured by the performance index. Robustness may be demonstrated by doing sensitivity analysis on system parameters, including the speed control parameter, GDB, GRC, and random load perturbation, for substantial changes. Moreover, the system’s performance has been assessed, considering the delay in communication, which significantly degrades the performance. Extensive simulations have shown that the fuzzy-based FOPID controller surpasses other controllers in terms of resilience and accuracy. Therefore, it may be considered a practical solution to the load frequency control problem.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Influence of DC-Link Inductor Design on Adjustable Speed Drive Performance
abstract: DC-link filter in Adjustable Speed Drives (ASDs) with a diode bridge rectifier typically includes a DC-link capacitor and an inductor, which can be positioned either on the AC side or within the DC-link itself. In industrial drives, the inductor is more commonly placed in the DC-link due to its lower voltage drop compared to an AC-side configuration. The shape of the laminations in the core of a DC-link inductor (also known as DC-coil) is a crucial design element, as it significantly affects the magnetic properties, efficiency, and overall performance of the inductor. Selecting the appropriate lamination shape is essential for optimizing the magnetic flux path, minimizing losses, and fitting the physical constraints of the inductor. This work analyzes the commonly used EI core shape, highlighting its challenges, and demonstrates how the UI core shape can address these issues effectively.

articleTitle: PI Control Design Using Padula and Visioli Method for Renewable Integrated Microgrid
abstract: The frequency control in islanded microgrids is one of the major challenges due to the interconnection of stochastic renewable sources. This work aims to enhance grid stability and reliability while maximizing renewable energy utilization. This presented work considered a renewable source-enabled islanded microgrid. Further, the mathematical model derived is of seventh order. Then, it is approximated as first-order plus time delay (FOPDT) form using reaction curve method. The suitable proportional-integral (PI) control design for proposed FOPDT model is presented to resolve load frequency issues. To achieve this, PI controller is tuned using the Padula and Visioli tuning approach. The analysis of presented control design approach is done by presenting the step responses and frequency deviation curve analysis for FOPDT modeled islanded microgrid. The detailed description of data of time domain analysis of microgrid model and approximated model under with and without controller are analyzed. The findings indicate that this research holds significant implications for control design for operation of resilient and sustainable microgrid systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive hybrid MPPT algorithms for grid connected PV system with solar irradiance and temperature variation
abstract: This study focuses on advancing the performance of grid-tied solar photovoltaic (PV) systems through the development of adaptive Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) strategies. Instead of conventional approaches, the research employs cutting-edge learning algorithms to enhance the system’s ability to harvest maximum power in dynamically changing environmental conditions.The effectiveness of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems that use an MPPT algorithm based on artificial neural networks (ANN) is examined in this study. This study looks at three different possible environmental states: (1) varying solar irradiance for a constant temperature; (2) varying temperatures for a constant irradiance; and (3) varying temperatures and irradiances simultaniously. Simulation results, executed using Matlab/Simulink, demonstrate the effectiveness of these intelligent algorithms in achieving superior power generation across a spectrum of environmental conditions. The proposed algorithm outperforms the aforementioned MPPT techniques in a number of important respects, including its rapid dynamic response time, low steady-state power oscillations, high power production efficiency, and ability to function effectively in environments with a great deal of environmental complexity.

articleTitle: Maximum solar power point tracking using Artificial hummingbird algorithm
abstract: In order to excerpt optimal green energy from intermittent solar irradiance, this work proposes a soft-computing-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique for solar powered panels. At the beginning, a MATLAB model is designed for the proposed technique considering the solar photovoltaic array, battery, and DC-DC converter. The design parameters were estimated for the available hardware specifications and simulated with conventional Perturb & Observe MPPT technique. The Simulink model was also tested with some contemporary MPPT techniques, like Fuzzy logic control, Particle swarm optimization and Artificial hummingbird algorithm (AHA). The performance of the proposed AHA is found superior by comparative analysis. Further the hardware prototype of the test system is developed with the help of necessary components and accessories. The hardware model is tested under different scenarios of irradiance using proposed AHA based MPPT technique for its validation and the responses are reported.

articleTitle: CNN with Attention Mechanism for Accurate Faulty Line Localization in High Impedance Fault Scenarios with Distributed Generators
abstract: The global power shortage has led to the widespread deployment of grid-integrated distributed energy resources or generators (DERs). A dependable and continuous power supply requires the protection of power systems, which have grown increasingly complex due to the integration of more dispersed generation. The most crucial aspect of complicated power sys-tem protection is precise and accurate faulty line or section localization. Modern power networks have bidirectional power flow and low magnitude of fault current due to high impedance fault (HIF) with integrated DERs, making conventional fault analysis approaches inappropriate. This study presented a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network with Attention Mechanism (CNN-AM) model that uses end-to-end deep learning for faulty line localization tasks. This automated methodology yields excellent accuracy and enhanced reliability, unlike machine learning, which necessitates preprocessing and human participation. Tests are conducted on various fault-simulated data sets on a grid with three distributed generators built into it. A Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind turbine, Solar Photovoltaic (PV), and Diesel Generator together serve as the distributed generators. The proposed CNN with AM model provides better accuracy in the presence of adversarial vulnerability for faulty line localization. Using our proposed model, 10-fold cross-validation yielded 99.03% accuracy for faulty line Localization. The proposed model compares with various existing deep learning models and performs outstandingly. Real-time data from the OPAL-RT simulator has been used to validate the proposed model, which shows its robustness.

articleTitle: Coordinated Electric Vehicle Charging Strategy for Self-Sustained Office Parking Lots
abstract: The rapid increase in electric vehicle (EV) adoption poses significant challenges for the current distribution system, which may struggle to accommodate the high EV charging demand. Existing EV charging infrastructure requires substantial charging times, ranging from 30 minutes to several hours, exceeding the refueling time for traditional gasoline vehicles. Eventually, EVs will undergo overnight home charging in the low-voltage residential area. This concentrated, uncoordinated EV charging will superimpose on residential demand and may coincide with the system peak. This study introduces the planning of office parking lots (OPLs) integrated with distributed energy resources (DERs) to shift the EV charging demand over the daytime. A Coordinated EV charging (CEVC) strategy is proposed to efficiently utilize DERs to minimize the energy transaction with the grid by varying the EV charging power to closely follow the solar generation. Further, the proposed strategy is compared with uncoordinated EV charging in terms of peak demand, energy exchange with the grid, and operational cost.

articleTitle: A Sigmoid Function Based Improved Observer for PV-Battery fed Sensorless PMaSyRM Driven Light Electric Vehicle
abstract: This paper presents a light electric vehicle (LEV) integrated with a solar photovoltaic (SPV) array. A bidirectional DC-DC (BDDC) converter is used to maintain the DC-link voltage and charging of the battery. The cascaded PI controllers are used to maintain the voltage and current of the LEV battery. The battery is charged via BDDC when solar insolation is available or through regeneration when brakes are applied. Otherwise, the battery supplies power to the permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor while the LEV is cruising or accelerating. For the estimation of speed and hence rotor position for vector control, the sigmoid function-based sliding mode observer (SMO) technique is used. In the traditional SMO technique, there is a chattering problem because of the discontinuous control function. In this paper, this problem is addressed with a sigmoid function. The speed and position are estimated with the SMO, which is used to generate pulses for the three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) through hysteresis current control. The presented system is simulated in MATLAB Simulink-based platform. The Vehicle dynamics and driving cycle techniques are used to analyze the performance of the overall system control. Simulated results showing the satisfactory performance of the BDDC, sigmoid function-based SMO and sensorless vector control technique for driving cycle-based operation of LEV.

Author Keywords: Permanent Magnet assisted Synchronous reluctance Motor (PMaSyRM)

articleTitle: Multi-Population based Hippopotamus Optimization Algorithm for Design of Switched Reluctance Motor for Enhanced Thermal Performance
abstract: Light Electric Vehicles (LEVs), such as e-rickshaws and e-autos, are critical for reducing urban air pollution but face thermal management challenges due to frequent stops and starts and the urban heat island effect. This paper analyzes temperature rise in Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs), which are suitable for LEVs due to their better heat dissipation capabilities. Hippopotamus optimization (HO) algorithm is presented first and then coupled with multi-population strategy. The proposed multi-population based hippopotamus optimization (MPHO) algorithm is compared with HO algorithm on CEC test suit and the convergence curves on selected functions are presented. MPHO algorithm is applied to the design of SRM for enhanced thermal performance. First local sensitivity analysis is carried out and the decision variables are identified to which temperature rise is most sensitive. A response surface model (RSM) is developed in conjugation with latin hypercube sampling (LHS) to evaluate objective function (temperature rise) and constraints (output power and efficiency). Finally, HO and MPHO algorithms are applied to the design of SRM and optimal design points are obtained. It is observed that MPHO performs better than HO algorithm and gives better results.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of the PLL for the Control of Solar-PV System Interfaced with Low Voltage Weak Grid
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of adverse increases in grid impedance on the stability of phase-locked Loop (PLL) in grid-connected PhotoVoltaic (PV) systems. A weak grid is characterized by limited short-circuit capacity, leading to voltage instability and sensitivity to fluctuations in power generation. Understanding PLL dynamics amidst these conditions is critical for ensuring the reliability and resilience of grid-connected PV systems. The mathematical modeling evaluates how control loop interaction disturbs PLL stability during a weak grid. The small signal stability analysis helps reveal the stability of PLL. The outcomes contribute to the scholarly discourse on weak grid conditions in renewable energy systems, aiding in developing strategies to fortify system stability and grid integration. The simulation studies show the stability analysis of the PLL during a weak grid condition from 0.4s to 0.6s using MATLAB®/SIMULINK. The results are as per the standards of IEEE 519-2022. Further, the simulated results are verified using the Hardware in Loop(HIL) results.

articleTitle: Investigation of Shunt Active Power Filter for Power Quality Improvement in Distribution System
abstract: In distribution systems, the load has been a unexpected increase or decreases and it is like as nonlinear loads so the load draw non-sinusoidal currents from the utility mains and causes the reactive power load, harmonics and high neutral currents that occurs the power quality problem in electrical distribution systems. Most power quality problem created in distribution systems are due to the nonlinear load and fast switching of power electronic devices. Shunt active filter based on current controlled PWM converters are seen as a most viable solution. In this paper, a shunt active power filter (SAPF) with PI controller is used. Current controlled voltage source converter topology is used in this SAPF. The quality and performance of SAPF depend on design of power converter, DC voltage control strategy, the method implemented to generate reference command and generation of switching pulses. For reference command generation Unit Active Power Component Theory (APCT) is used and for DC voltage control PI controller is used. A hysteresis current controller is used to generate the switching pulses. The detailed simulation study of work has been carried out in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Keywords—Power Quality, SAPF, Distribution System, APCT

articleTitle: Selection of Stator Pole Tip for Torque Ripple Reduction of Switched Reluctance Motor
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motors are gaining prominence in various industrial and domestic applications due to their robustness and simplicity. However, one of the major challenges associated with switched reluctance motors is the high torque ripple. It is a prominent issue in switched reluctance motors, which leads to undesirable vibrations and noise, impacting the motor’s overall performance. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts in the optimization of switched reluctance motors and provides valuable insights for engineers and researchers involved in motor design. This work focuses on the selection of the stator pole tip to mitigate torque ripple in switched reluctance motors. Using electromagnetic analysis and simulation, the influence of variation in stator pole tip on torque ripple reduction is investigated. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of stator pole tip variation in reducing torque ripple, thereby improving the overall performance and stability of switched reluctance motors. These findings underscore the effectiveness of this design modification technique in the reduction of torque ripple without adversely affecting other motor performance parameters.

articleTitle: Non-Isolated On-board Battery Charger with Wide Output Voltage Range for e-Transportation
abstract: In electric transportation, on-board chargers (OBCs) alleviate worries about the need to often charge the battery packs because different electric vehicle (EV) engine types have varying requirements for input power supplies and battery pack voltages. A single-phase, non-isolated OBC for electric vehicles is presented in this paper. Primary benefit of this on-board charger (OBC) is its ability to maintain excellent input power quality across a wide range of output voltage conversions, which is essential for efficiently charging electric vehicle (EV) batteries. Specifically, it can accommodate an output voltage range of 150 V to 400 V , making it adaptable to different kinds of batteries and charging conditions. This wide output voltage range ensures that an OBC can handle different EV battery specifications and charging requirements, providing reliable and efficient charging performance. To facilitate charging of a broad range of EVs, a controller is designed that maintains on grid side’s unity power factor, while controlling output voltage buck and boost operations with a seamless transition. Performance of the proposed charger is verified using MATLAB simulation for an input ac supply of 230 V and is compared with different topologies available in the literature.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbances and Detection Methods: A Brief Review
abstract: Power quality (PQ) issues are becoming diversified due to non-linear nature of loads, high renewable energy (RE) integration to grids, and extensive use of power electronics-based devices. Accurate detection and classification of PQ events will help in ensuring good quality of power being supplied to customers. Knowledge of existing methods will help in development of advanced techniques of PQ detection and classification. Hence, this paper presents a brief overview of PQ events, different stages of automatic PQ recognition, methods applied for detection and categorization of PQ disturbances, and impact of RE on PQ. Relative strengths and weaknesses of commonly used PQ detection and classification methods are presented at the end of paper. This review is helpful for designers, researchers, and engineers working in the field of power quality.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Constrained Adaptive Coordination scheme in a Microgrid Considering Different Network Topologies
abstract: The integration of distributed generators (DGs) has significantly impacted utility grid operations, making them more complex and affecting protection systems performance. Issues include bidirectional power flow, voltage profile fluctuations, and dynamic behaviour. Transient stability analysis helps to determine critical clearing time (CCT), which is the maximum time allowed for generator stability to be maintained. In this paper, relay coordination is carried out considering different network topologies that occur due to contingencies of sources as well as lines while maintaining the CCT of the system. A few contingencies have been considered, resulting in the formation of eleven topologies of the microgrid, which are grouped into three clusters using K-means clustering based on their average operating time. The optimal relay settings for all clusters were identified while complying with the CCT criteria using the Genetic Algorithm (GA). The proposed relay coordination scheme is verified on the 7-bus microgrid which is the distribution part of the modified IEEE-14 bus test system.

articleTitle: Identification of High Impedance Faults Utilizing Recurrence Plots
abstract: This paper presents a systematic approach to detecting High Impedance Faults (HIFs) in medium voltage distribution networks using recurrence plots and machine learning. We first simulate 1150 internal faults, including 300 HIFs, 1000 external faults, and 40 normal conditions using the PSCAD/EMTDC software. Key features are extracted from the 3-phase differential currents using wavelet coefficients, which are then converted into recurrence matrices. A multi-stage classification framework is employed, where the first classification stage identifies internal faults, and the second stage distinguishes HIFs from other internal faults. The framework is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Tree-based classifiers, particularly Random Forest and Decision Tree, achieve superior performance, with 99.24% accuracy in the first stage and 98.26% in the second. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating recurrence analysis with machine learning for fault detection in power distribution networks.

articleTitle: Role of Flexibility in Thermal Plants for Energy transition
abstract: The Power sector across the world is undergoing a transformative shift towards cleaner and more sustainable energy sources. This research paper delves into the intricate dynamics of the evolving energy landscape in Indian power sector, focusing on different sector related parameters viz. load profile analysis, flexible operation insights, and future actions for coal-based thermal plants. The analysis recommends that storage additions, including Pumped Hydro and Lithium-ion batteries, have potential to mitigate the requirement for flexible operation, which is projected to reach approximately 1% (presently around 0.2%) by 2030. Acknowledging the limitations of human control for high flexible generation needs the digitalization of coal-based thermal plants and gas plants emerges as a key necessity for achieving the desired levels of flexibility. Implementation of ancillary services through flexible operations stands out as a revenue-generating strategy for the electricity sector. Addressing future actions for coal-based thermal plants, the analysis assumes that all plants can engage in flexible operation. However, considering the aging infrastructure, particularly with 52 GW (20% of the total) expected to be over 25 years old by 2030, challenges may arise. Sufficient storage capacity, such as Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), proves instrumental in mitigating ramp rate requirements posed by older plants, while research and development efforts should focus on improving boiler response times for enhanced flexibility.As India navigates its energy transition, this research provides valuable insights for policymakers, industry stakeholders, and researchers to strategically plan and implement measures that ensure a resilient and sustainable electricity sector.

articleTitle: WOA based Optimal TIDF Controller for Time Delayed System
abstract: This manuscript presents a novel methodology to effectively control time-delayed systems. In this work, authors have proposed a Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) tuned Tilt Integral Derivative Controller with Derivative Filter (TIDF) specifically designed for regulating time-delayed systems characterized by 4th order dynamics. The efficacy of the proposed method has been thoroughly verified by comparing its transient response specifications with those of existing approaches documented in the literature. This comparative analysis demonstrates that the WOA-tuned TIDF controller offers superior performance in terms of transient response, highlighting its suitability for the intended application. Additionally, the robustness of the proposed algorithm has been rigorously tested under conditions involving variable time delays, which are a common and challenging aspect of real-world systems. The results of these tests indicate that the WOA-tuned TIDF controller not only achieves a better transient response but also maintains stability and robustness across different scenarios. Consequently, the proposed methodology provides a reliable and effective solution for controlling time-delayed systems, ensuring both enhanced performance and resilience in various industrial and technological applications.

articleTitle: Steady-State and State-Space Analysis of Two Switched-Impedance Network Enhanced-Boost Series-Z-source Inverter
abstract: In this broadside, steady-state as well as state-space analysis of the enhanced-boost series-Z-source inverter (EB-SZSI) is supported out. Analogous to predictable EB-(q)ZSIs, this projected inverter analysis situs keeps identical high voltage lift at low-slung duty ratio and high modulation index to afford healthier eminence output wave shape besides diminish the switch stress. Additionally, the proposed topology provides less voltage across the capacitors. Consequently, inferior grade capacitors can be hand-me-down to condense the size, cost, and weight of the system. Besides, akin to EB-qZSI, this anticipated topology is able to unravel the unruly of starting inrush current, shares common ground with source and bridge inverter. This paper presents the steady-state analysis and compares with conventional ZSI, SL-ZSI, EB-ZSI, and EB-qZSIs. Moreover, the state-space analysis of the proposed topology is also carried out. Finally, the validation of theoretical analysis of the proposed inverter topology is verified in MATLAB/Simulink with 60 V dc input voltage and 110 Vrms as output voltage.

articleTitle: Binary Quasi-Oppositional Brown-bear Optimization Algorithm Based Maximization of Measurement Redundancy through Strategic Placement of Phasor Measurement Units
abstract: A phasor measuring unit (PMU) is the equipment that measures the power network voltage and current. It measures the phase angle and amplitude of an electrical quantity, which are referred to as phasors. The measured phasors carry a time stamp since the waveforms measured from the PMU are synchronized with the global time standard using the global positioning system (GPS). PMUs give a thorough and precise analysis of the power quality over a large geographic grid. The system operator can determine from the data collected whether the voltage, current, and frequency continue to lie within prescribed tolerances. The number of PMUs must be reduced due to their high cost, and their placement must be optimized to attain full system observability. For optimal PMU placement, other aspects, including network topology, generating sources, and measurement redundancy, should also be taken into account. In this paper, the binary quasi-oppositional Brown-Bear optimization algorithm is used to obtain the optimal locations of PMU. The algorithm is evaluated on several IEEE test systems, and when compared to other methods, the attained results appear to be better.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison between Solid Oxide Fuel Cell-Battery and PEM Fuel Cell-Battery Powered Locomotives for application in Indian Railways
abstract: The paper aims to analyze the feasibility of replacing the diesel locomotives with solid oxide fuel cell-battery-hybrid energy system (SOFC-battery-HES) to drive the inter-city passenger (ICP) trains in India. For this analysis, a comparison of the SOFC-battery-HES with an equivalent proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC)-battery-HES is carried out in terms of four performance indices namely, capital cost (CC), operational cost (OC), durability, and their environmental impact with respect to carbon emissions. For cost comparison, a design optimization model (DOM) is firstly formulated to determine the ratings of the SOFC and battery such that the designed SOFC-battery-HES can supply the power demand of ICP trains. The objective of optimization is to minimize the total cost which is the summation of the CC and OC of the SOFC-battery-HES.
