To regulate the distribution of load in the HES, a rule-based energy management strategy (EMS) is developed and is used as a subroutine in the particle swarm optimization-based solution approach to solve the DOM. The CC and OC of the SOFC-battery-HES obtained through optimization are now compared with the corresponding costs of an equivalent PEMFC-battery-HES. Besides cost comparison, the durability and carbon emissions of the HESs when advocated in Indian Railways are also examined. The simulation study is carried out using the data of the diesel locomotive type WDM-7 and the drive cycle of a currently operating ICP train of Indian Railways.

articleTitle: Design, Implementation, and Performance Analysis of Average and Hysteresis Current Controlled Non-Isolated Boost PFC for Induction Heating
abstract: The presence of a filtered diode rectifier in the power stage of an Induction heater (IH) inevitably lowers the power factor and distorts the input current waveform of the utility. This leads to reduced efficiency and interferes with the functioning of other line-connected equipment. This paper attempts to improve the input power factor and regulate the line current harmonics within electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards. In this work, a non-isolated boost converter is operated in continuous conduction mode (CCM) to provide a precise and ripple-free DC voltage to the series resonant inverter of an induction heating system. A two-loop controller is designed with an outer voltage loop for regulating the power and an inner current loop for shaping the input current. The inductor current of the boost converter is controlled by Average current mode (ACM) control and Variable hysteresis current control (HCC) methods and their performance is gauged in terms of total harmonic distortion (THD) and power factor improvement. The control strategies are developed and implemented in an FPGA-based rapid prototyping tool and an induction heating system experimentally validates their performance. The results obtained show the superiority of the ACM (THD 2.4%,4.3%) over HCC (THD 3.02%,6.3%) in simulation and experimentally both.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Solar-Grid Interfaced EV Charging Infrastructure Using STF Controller
abstract: In this work, we investigate a new unique way for charging batteries from renewable energy systems and grids with extra power, denoted as excess power. This technique aims to optimise battery charging/discharging and reduce dependent on the power grid. The essence of this technique revolves around self-tuning filters (STF) that offer undistorted fundamental value load current. Using this strategy, excess power charges the battery in an efficient manner. There were probable advantages of this sort of setups (i) decreased dependency on the central grid (ii) increased exploitation of renewable energy sources (iii)) Longer battery life is accomplished by using optimal charging strategies. The report continues by outlining probable possibilities for future research, such as evaluating the integration of this system with energy management platforms and testing its scalability for more large applications.

articleTitle: A Passive Loss of Mains Detection Scheme for Inverter based Distribution Energy Resources
abstract: Distributed energy resources based on renewable energy have significantly developed over the past few decades because of the need to include environmentally friendly energy sources due to their advantages of clean and non-exhaustible nature of energy. Due to its unpredictable and uncertain nature, this form of generation poses technological difficulties in terms of operation and control. The integration of these distributed generating systems to the main grid comes with certain challenges, out of which Islanding/ Loss of Mains detection is of prior importance. A passive loss of mains detection technique for inverter-based distribution energy resources is proposed in this paper. The developed method constructs the islanding detection indices by considering the three-phase voltage and frequency at the Point of Common Coupling. An extensive assessment of the proposed method is conducted by using PSCAD/EMTDC simulations and field data. The proposed method has less Non-Detection Zone and is able to determine all types of events accurately. It is observed that the method is superior in terms of accuracy and speed when compared to other currently available techniques.

articleTitle: Single Inductor Dual Output DC-DC Converter
abstract: This paper presents a single-inductor, dual-output DC-DC converter. Conventional two-single output converters are available to obtain dual output voltages, however they have drawback of being expensive and large in volume. Therefore, the SIDO (unidirectional) focuses to reduce component count and cost. This work outlines and evaluates the boost-type SIDO converter. Furthermore, the use of PV as a source, plus a DC-AC converter/inverter, is proposed to supply power to the grid. The implementation of a closed loop structure to reduce the interdependency of two switches is further explored.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of False Data Injection Attacks in Power System Operations
abstract: This paper performs the impact analysis of a random Load Redistribution False Data Injection (LR-FDI) attacks on Security Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) operations of power system. A successful LR-FDI attack on SCED in power system may cause disruptions in logic parameters of controllers setting, destabilizing the power market by generation imbalance, and, false state estimation. DC-OPF based SCED problem under the LR-FDI attack scenario is formulated to analyze the feasibility and consequences. Problem formulated is tested on IEEE 24-RTS system, and solved on GAMS optimization platform using CONOPT solver.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Optimization Techniques for Model Order Reduction
abstract: Model order reduction (MOR) plays a key role in simplifying complex dynamic systems while retaining essential characteristics. This study investigates five advanced optimization techniques for MOR: the jaya optimization algorithm, particle swarm optimization (PSO), grey wolf optimization (GWO), genetic algorithm (GA), and bat algorithm. Two sample systems are selected to demonstrate order reduction. Each algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated based on its ability to minimize system errors and sustain critical system dynamics. To comprehensively assess the optimization approaches, the study incorporates several performance metrics, including system stability, integral-absolute-error (IAE), and integral-squared-error (ISE). The results highlight the strengths and limitations of each technique in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of Unipolar Pulse Width Modulated Voltage Source Inverter
abstract: This paper presents a study on the modeling and control of a Unipolar Pulse Width Modulated (PWM) Voltage Source Inverter (VSI). Specifically focusing on current control in a unipolar PWM single-phase inverter, the paper rigorously derives and analyzes the transfer function for current control. A Proportional-Integral (PI) controller is designed to achieve desired performance metrics. Simulation and experimental results validate the efficacy of the proposed controller, demonstrating its robustness in tracking reference current under varying circuit parameters. Additionally, the observed behavior aligns with theoretical predictions, particularly concerning the phase difference between reference and actual currents at higher modulating frequencies. However, analysis reveals a consistent phase displacement in the closed-loop system, suggesting the persistence of some phase difference between input and output signals unless the frequency is zero.

articleTitle: The Impact Analysis of Different Activation Functions on CNN-based Reduced OPF
abstract: The Optimal Power Flow (OPF) obtains economic generation dispatch considering transmission line constraints. The solution of OPF for a large power system is computationally complex due to many variables and constraints. OPF with only critical constraints called Reduced OPF (ROPF) is used to reduce computational complexity without compromising the accuracy of the solution. Suitable deep-learning algorithms can identify critical constraints. The performance of such deep learning algorithms relies on activation functions. However, there is less focus on deep learning-based ROPF and impact analysis of activation function on deep learning-based ROPF. Therefore, this paper proposes a CNN-based ROPF using different activation functions. The CNN algorithm is used to predict the critical constraints and hyperparameters of CNN are optimized with the Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimization algorithm. The OPF is performed using the Gurobi optimizer. The performance of different activation functions like Exponential Linear Unit (ELU), Leaky Rectified Linear Unit (Leaky ReLU), and Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) are analyzed to identify the best one. The performance analysis is carried out on the IEEE 73 bus system. The results show that CNN with PReLU performs better than other activation functions. Also, significant time is saved with deep learning-based ROPF.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Dual DC motor control module for Remote tilt control of Antenna
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a dual DC motor control module for remote antenna tilt control. Utilizing an STM32 microcontroller, the system provides precise control over motor speed and direction, ensuring accurate antenna positioning essential for optimal signal reception. The DRV8802 motor driver is employed to achieve robust performance in low-power applications, providing reliability and efficiency. The control scheme optimizes motor speed regulation through advanced algorithms, incorporating closed-loop control strategies to enhance the system's responsiveness and stability. Real-time feedback is achieved using hall-effect sensors, which offer precise measurements of motor position and speed, ensuring high accuracy in control and positioning. Power management within the system is facilitated by an efficient buck converter design, ensuring stable power supply to the motors and minimizing energy consumption. The hardware design includes protective features such as overcurrent and thermal shutdown to enhance the system's durability.The control module's effectiveness is validated through extensive simulations and practical implementations, demonstrating its capability to maintain precise and reliable antenna positioning under various operating conditions. The system's scalability and flexibility make it suitable for a wide range of applications in communication technology.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Radial Electromagnetic Bearings using Measured Magnetic Characteristics of Core Materials over Wide Frequency Range
abstract: Radial electromagnetic bearings (EMBs) provide friction-free and lubrication-free support to high-speed rotors against various radial disturbance forces including their self-weights. The EMB performance critically depends on the high-frequency behaviour of the core material used. This paper investigates the high-frequency magnetic characteristics of an Si-Fe steel, namely 50C470, for an 8-pole radial EMB, used to support a 30,000-rpm rotor. The B-H loops of 50C470 are obtained experimentally at eleven different frequencies between 50 Hz and 1000 Hz, and for peak flux densities up to 1.5 T at each frequency. The experimental data are used as material inputs to perform Finite Element Analysis (FEA) for performance evaluation of certain radial EMB design. The influence of the magnetic core material on the air-gap flux-density distribution, radial-force-density distribution, and the radial force versus control-current characteristics along x- and y-directions are demonstrated. Significant reduction is observed in the peak sinusoidal force along any given direction due to finite core permeability. High-magnitude control currents are shown to produce significant third harmonic in the force along a given direction, and prominent fourth harmonic in the total radial force on the rotor. The findings are useful to improve the design, modelling, operation and control of radial EMB.

articleTitle: Introduction of Si-nanowire in Four-terminal (4T) Tandem Solar Cell to Improve Efficiency Share
abstract: The main challenge in commercializing multi-junction tandem solar cells is the lack of economic viability, primarily due to the poor performance of the bottom cell caused by optical coupling. The study introduces a Si-nanowire (SiNW) array as the bottom cell of a GaAs//Si-nanowire tandem architecture to enhance the efficiency of the bottom cell in a four-terminal (4T) configuration. The work compares the bulk-Si cell and SiNW for the bottom cell. Simulations of the SiNW bottom cell incorporate two key features from experimental data: increased surface area for improved photon absorption and increased surface recombination. Enhanced photon absorption in the SiNW array allows it to utilize the filtered spectra from the GaAs top cell, boosting the efficiency share and making the tandem architecture more cost-effective. The SiNW bottom cell shares 40.5% of the 4T tandem efficiency (30.85%), leading a path-way to introduce the SiNW array as the bottom cell to produce efficient Si-based tandem cells.

articleTitle: Robust Control of WPT System With Selected Weighting Function Considering Parameter Perturbations
abstract: H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller is used to improve the performance of inductive power transfer (IPT) system. However, the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> design considers nominal plant while designing the controller, so the desired performance may not be guaranteed. To improve the IPT dynamic performance, in this paper a µ-controller is designed. Generalized state-space model is used to get the IPT system transfer function and its effect due to perturbation. Uncertain model is developed using multiplicative uncertainty and then used in µ-controller design. Performance of IPT is simulated both with "µ" and "H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>" controller and then compared.

articleTitle: Minimum DC-Link Energy Storage Requirement of Half-Bridge Interleaved based Integrated On-board EV Charger
abstract: The simplest onboard integrated electric vehicle chargers, which utilize the same circuitry for both traction and charging purposes, fundamentally consist of three-interleaved half-bridges and split DC-link capacitors. This paper presents the calculation of the minimum DC-link capacitance for the front-end half-bridge AC-DC converter. Using the calculated value allows for significant size and cost reductions by employing this minimum capacitance. The proposed design can be applied to the cascade connection of converters, where the load converter is characterised as a constant power load. The minimum capacitance value is derived as a function of the mains voltage and frequency, the maximum power transferred to the load converter, and the desired DC-link voltage. The resulting capacitance is approximately four times smaller than that obtained through conventional design methods. Moreover, theoretical analysis are verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Cost-Effective Data-Driven Approaches for Electricity Theft Detection
abstract: Electricity theft poses a significant challenge to utilities and power grids worldwide, leading to substantial financial losses, increased operational costs, and overloading of electrical networks. This not only compromises the efficiency and reliability of power supply systems but also increases the risk of grid failures and safety hazards for maintenance personnel. Despite various efforts to mitigate electricity theft, including manual detection methods, hardware-based detection systems, and data-driven approaches, the issue remains prevalent and difficult to fully eliminate. The existing data-driven techniques, particularly traditional methods such as Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Long Short-Term Memory networks, and Decision Trees, have shown limitations in terms of accuracy, precision, sensitivity, recall, and specificity, making them less effective for real-time detection and prevention of electricity theft.This paper aims to address these challenges by exploring advanced data-driven methods, specifically deep learning techniques, to enhance the accuracy and reliability of electricity theft detection systems. By applying Convolutional Neural Networks, Wide and Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, and Time Series Forecasting alongside machine learning approaches, the research aims to overcome the limitations of traditional models. These advanced methods provide improved performance in detecting theft, offering better precision and sensitivity in comparison to fundamental approaches. The study presents a detailed comparison of different models, highlighting the advantages of deep learning and time series-based forecasting in improving the overall detection process, with the goal of contributing to more robust and efficient electricity theft detection mechanisms for modern power grids.

articleTitle: Analysis of Maximum Correntropy Criterion-based Algorithms for the Control of Shunt Active Power Filter
abstract: Shunt active power filters (SAPFs) are a highly efficient and practical solution for mitigating issues related to power quality. The objective of the SAPF is to produce and introduce the necessary electrical current into the power system to remove any unwanted harmonic distortions in the load and achieve a supply power factor of unity. This paper applies three Maximum Correntropy Criterion (MCC) -based algorithms, namely conventional MCC, adaptive kernel width maximum correntropy criterion (AMCC), and switch kernel width maximum correntropy criterion (SMCC), to operate SAPF. Analysis is based on filtering capability, response time, mathematical complexity, and THD in source current. Both open loop and closed loop working of proposed algorithms has been investigated and verified using simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Backup Protection of the Transmission Network Under Stressed Conditions
abstract: The complex operating modes of the power transmission network have inadvertently increased the vulnerability of relay mal-function due to stressed conditions such as load encroachment and power swing etc. These conditions can trigger cascading outages, posing significant challenges in maintaining grid stability. Unintended operations of distance relays have been identified as a major factor in cascading outages and significant power system blackouts. To address this, enhancing backup protection to detect these stressed conditions has therefore become a top priority. A proposed backup protection scheme for detecting stressed conditions leverages the Rate of Change of Impedance Angle (ROCOIA) and effectively differentiates between internal and external faults using the Super-Imposed Current Angle Difference (SICAD). In contrast to conventional protection relays that isolate faulted components, this backup scheme initiates corrective actions to stabilize the power system under stressed conditions. It also unblocks the distance relay during faults, thereby ensuring the overall integrity and reliability of the system across various stressed scenarios.

articleTitle: Performance and Stability Comparison of Grid Forming Inverters with Droop and VSG Controls for Autonomous Microgrids
abstract: Grid-forming inverters have become a prominent topic due to the increasing penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DER). This paper presents a comparative study of two grid-forming inverters controlled using both identical and differing Droop and Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) controls, operating in autonomous mode. The comparison focuses on settling time, peak deviation and stability limit while ensuring equal active power sharing in a steady state. This paper concludes that the system operating with identical Droop control provides less settling time but is less stable as compared to the Droop-VSG controlled system. The analysis is conducted using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Computing Framework for SoC Estimation using On-device Learning
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) are the most widespread technology used in smart grids to promote grid reliability and store excess energy. The BESSs rely on a single, non-measurable parameter called State-of-Charge (SoC) for decision-making and is challenging to obtain. The existing SoC estimation methods have drawbacks, including a lack of real-time correction features and generalizability across different systems. Working to mitigate the aforementioned challenges, this paper presents a complete SoC estimation study with scalable hardware design, machine learning-based SoC estimator, and application of different computing paradigms, i.e., node, edge, and cloud devices. Firstly, a two-cell lithium-ion battery kit is designed for charging-discharging, facilitating data recording, and utilizing a Pi Pico device to send data over WiFi. An LSTM model is deployed in Raspberry Pi 4, which saves upcoming data from Pico, runs inference, and sends the inference to the local build cloud server at the monitoring station over WiFi. Lastly, the On-device learning feature has also been incorporated to tackle inaccuracy, promoting the robustness, adaptability, and reliability of the inference system. The results demonstrated high accuracy, achieving a R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9969 on the testing dataset, and also highlighted the importance of the adaptability feature incorporated in the framework.

articleTitle: Optimal Structural Robustness to Enhance Transmission Line Resilience for HILP Events
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of High Impact Low Probability (HILP) extreme weather events are posing significant threats to the resilience of power System. This paper proposes enhancement of resilience of transmission lines by determining optimal structural robustness by modifying material strength and design parameters under varying wind conditions. The Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) method evaluates the initial failure probabilities of transmission lines at different wind speeds. A robust optimization framework is formulated using an Interior-Point (IP) Algorithm to maximize the resilience level of the transmission system. The results demonstrated on IEEE 57-bus system shows that the optimized parameters significantly improve the resilience of the network, reducing the failure of transmission lines under different wind speed conditions. This study provides an insight into the measures to sustain the impact of wind by suggesting robustness of transmission lines against severe weather events.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Two-Level Three-Phase Voltage Source Converter using SiC MOSFET for Grid-Connected EV Charging Systems
abstract: Air pollution, global warming and other such environmental issues are causing the governments, manufacturers and consumers to move towards electrification of transportation. Most manufacturers are trying to build better and more efficient electric vehicles (EVs) as it acts as a sustainable alternative to traditional internal combustion engines. In this context, designing better power electronic converters is pivotal. The design of a SiC MOSFET-based charger with two- stages for EV applications is discussed in this paper. The presented charger utilizes a three-phase, two-level voltage source converter as the front end and a buck converter as the back-end stage of the charger. The charger is used for implementing various battery charging modes, like charging under constant voltage and charging under constant current. The converter topology, control strategies, and design techniques employed to optimize performance under various conditions are detailed in this work. Using SiC MOSFET as the switching device gives the overall design an advantage over other Si counterparts because of SiC MOSFET’s low on-state resistance, strong thermal stability, and quick switching speed. MATLAB simulations and experimental implementation are done to confirm the design’s overall operation and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Multifunctional Frequency Adaptive Control Strategy of Grid Connected SPV System for Simultaneous Mitigation of Current Harmonics and Power Oscillations
abstract: This paper proposes a multifunctional frequency adaptive control approach for a three-phase single-stage grid connected solar photovoltaic (GCSPV) system. The proposed control strategy integrates a frequency-adaptive proportional multi-resonant (FAPMR) current controller, which effectively suppresses grid current harmonics in the presence of harmonically distorted grid voltage conditions caused by nonlinear loads. To enhance synchronization with the grid and simultaneously eliminate frequency oscillations, an improved second-order generalized integrator-based frequency locked loop (ISOGI-FLL) is incorporated with the proposed FAPMR controller. This strategy also mitigates oscillations in active and reactive power during unbalanced grid faults and improves the frequency adaptability of the GCSPV system during grid frequency variations. The proposed control strategy is implemented in the αβ reference frame, avoiding Park’s transformation, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity. Real-time digital simulations are executed with OPAL-RT OP4510 in a software-in-the-loop (SIL) environment to validate the efficacy of the proposed control strategy. Various adverse grid voltage conditions, including harmonically distorted voltages, unbalanced grid faults, and grid frequency variations are encompassed within these simulations.

articleTitle: Order Diminution of SEPIC Converters: Direct Truncation Methodology and Application
abstract: SEPIC converter is a versatile DC-to-DC converter that can adjust voltage levels both upwards and downwards. By featuring two inductors and two capacitors, the SEPIC converter operates as a fourth-order converter. Initially, a continuous conduction mode of operation (CCM) is taken into consideration when modeling SEPIC converter using the state space analysis (SSA) technique. A linearized interval model of SEPIC is obtained by putting SSA into execution and interval constituting of 10% variations is considered. For reducing the complexity of analysis process, an approximation of higher-order(HO) SEPIC converter is carried out. Direct truncation method is used to approximate the linearized transfer function of the HO system to a third order model and subsequently to a second order model. All of these models’ step, Bode, and impulse responses are provided for comparison, along with those for system. Based on evaluation of these responses, conclusion is derived on the efficiency and applicability of proposed method.

articleTitle: Exploring Future Sustainable Energy Resource - A Review on Diamond Batteries
abstract: Diamond batteries present a revolutionary approach to energy storage problems by utilizing the special qualities of both diamonds and radioisotopes, with the potential to produce long-lasting and maintenance-free power sources that might operate for millennia. This technique uses artificial diamonds embedded with radioactive isotopes such as carbon-14 or nickel-63 to operate through betavoltaic conversion. Space exploration, military hardware, medical implants, and Internet Of Things devices are the key applications of this technique. Prototypes with promising capabilities have been exhibited by businesses such as NDB Inc. and Betavolt Technology in recent breakthroughs. There are still challenges to overcome, though, including as expensive production costs, restricted power output, environmental concerns, and scalability problems. Despite these challenges, diamond batteries provide a revolutionary way to store energy and have the ability to recycle radioactive waste while producing clean and long-lasting power. As research advances, this sort of technology has the potential to transform energy solutions for a variety of industries by balancing innovation and sustainability. In a world where energy is becoming more and more important, the invention of diamond batteries is an ideal example of continuing searches for more eco-friendly and productive power sources.

articleTitle: Optimizing DER Hosting Capacity and Power Loss Minimization in Distribution System with GWO
abstract: The Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) are being integrated into the distribution system to utilize the renewable sources of energy and reducing carbon emissions. However, with increase in penetration of DERs, certain negative impacts are visible on distribution systems. The Hosting Capacity (HC) assessment facilitates the DER interconnection while ensuring compliance with operational limits. In this paper, an optimization-based approach is proposed to determine the locational HC of DERs such that the total active power losses in the system are reduced. The Gray Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is used for optimization. The proposed method is applied on IEEE 33-bus system. A Voltage Stability Index (VSI) based approach is also proposed to determine the feasibility of the solutions obtained for voltage stability. The suggested method offers appropriate locations for DER integration, resulting in optimal HC capacity with minimized losses. Furthermore, voltage stability is preserved under various loading scenarios.

articleTitle: EV User’s Charging Behaviour and its Impact on the Power Grid – A Case Study in Singapore
abstract: Singapore is increasingly embracing greener transportation options, marked by a growing number of Electric Vehicles (EVs) on its roads. Understanding the charging behavior of EV drivers is crucial to preparing Singapore’s power grid for the additional load. A survey was conducted to identify the factors influencing drivers' decisions to charge their vehicles. The collected data was analyzed using the statistical package for the social sciences (SPSS) to pinpoint dependent and independent variables affecting these decisions. Additionally, the study examined the impact of EV charging on the power grid and explored the potential of bi-directional chargers to mitigate peak load consumption. Survey findings reveal that cost-sensitive individuals tend to charge during off-peak hours (12 AM to 6 AM), while those less concerned with costs charge based on convenience and immediate need.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Clustering based Contingency Analysis Considering Renewable Energy Sources and Ancillary Services
abstract: With the proliferation of power grid interconnections and penetration of intermittent energy resources, the operations of modern power systems become more complex and dynamic. In addition, economic benefits and widespread transmission expansions have compelled the power systems to operate closer to their stability and thermal limits. If localized outages in one or more components of the power system violate the stability and thermal limits, the system may respond by a cascade of outages and even a system blackout. Therefore, contingency analysis has become a paramount tool for reliable and secure operation of power system network. The complexity associated with operation of such a larger network can be reduced by segregation of power network into smaller zones. So, in this paper hierarchical clustering technique is used to form zones and contingency analysis is done based on these zones. A case study is performed on the IEEE 14-bus system to show the effectiveness of hierarchical clustering based contingency analysis.

articleTitle: A Study of Static State Estimation of AC microgrid
abstract: State estimation process is used for estimating the microgrid’s parameters (voltage, current, and phase angles) and real-time operating conditions. Results from a number of mathematical algorithms and simulations are taken for the state estimation process. Before state estimation many problem were faced such as, inaccurate monitoring, poor control and stability, inefficient energy management etc. Now a days state estimation helps in improving reliability and enhanced monitoring and Control Operations. The reliability and efficacy of electrical power systems have significantly improved in recent years due to the broad adoption of AC microgrids. This paper explores the state estimation techniques for accurately determining the parameters of AC microgrids, which are useful for their optimal operation, control, and protection. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the various methodologies used in state estimation, including conventional based method’s, machine learning based approaches and simulations based approaches. Finally, the review identifies future research areas and highlights the importance of more robust and adaptable state estimation methods in order to improve AC microgrid efficiency.

articleTitle: Influence of Fast-Moving Cumulus Cloud on Power Quality of Emerging Grid-Tied Solar Farms with Heterogeneous Control Techniques: A Case Study
abstract: The international renewable energy agency (IRENA) estimates that, in the upcoming future, 90% of the world’s electricity will be from renewable energy sources. Among available sources, solar is gaining popularity because of its easy maintenance and availability. The unavoidable variability of solar irradiation can cause detrimental impacts on power grids. One of the main reasons for rapid irradiance transitions is fast-moving cumulus clouds. Impact of such clouds on power injected into the grid by solar farms and hence on the power quality is not well studied in literature. Temperature of solar panels, heterogeneous control methods followed by grid-tied inverters, and the strength of the bus bar at the point of common coupling (PCC) are the principal factors that decide the impact. This paper illustrates such an impact through simulation-based case studies conducted on an IEEE-9 bus system. Reactive power injection to the grid by the solar farms are considered, and case studies are conducted for various penetration levels of grid-following and grid-forming inverters. The results for the case studies can significantly contribute to the design and selection of flexible dispatch systems like energy storage.

articleTitle: A Review on Distributed Control Strategies in Cyber-Enabled Microgrids
abstract: Advanced control strategies are necessary for microgrids that integrate hybrid, AC, and DC systems to attain maximum efficiency and stability. A thorough analysis of distributed control strategies for cyber-enabled microgrid systems is provided in this paper, covering significant techniques such as droop control, model predictive control (MPC), event-triggered consensus control, heterogeneous consensus control, linear consensus control, and finite-time consensus control. The paper delves into the control challenges associated with these methodologies, emphasising the function of multi-agent systems (MAS) in enabling coordinated control and enhancing adaptability across various microgrid configurations. The study serves as an essential resource for improving and efficient microgrid operations by offering insights into the implementation and efficacy of various control systems.

articleTitle: A Stand-Alone System Utilizing Switch Inductor and Voltage Lift Based High Step-Up Converter
abstract: This paper explores the operating principle, performance evaluation, and benefits of a newly derived high-gain converter topology based on a switch inductor and voltage lift cell through theoretical analysis. Advantages of converter which include a single switch, easy control, high voltage gain and reduced voltage stress, are confirmed through MATLAB based simulations and experimental work. Its application is purposed in stand-alone photovoltaic (PV) and battery integrated system including a bi-directional DC-DC converter to maintain a constant 380V at the DC grid. The performance of the proposed PV and battery integrated system are explained, with a simulation model built for a 1289W PV array and a 722W resistive load. Performance is discussed for dynamic changes in irradiation. Results were obtained for dynamic changes in PV supply irradiation, ranging from 400 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 800 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Additionally, a low-power prototype hardware setup was developed to analyze the performance of the proposed high-gain converter and results were gathered under the supply voltage variations.

articleTitle: Flexible Droop Control Scheme of VSC-MTDC System
abstract: Managing power imbalance in contingency, like converter outage, is vital to Multiterminal Direct Current (MTDC) grid stability. This paper introduces a new flexible/variable droop regulation approach to provide an optimum distribution of power among droop-controlled converter stations as per their respective capacities as well as available headroom at the time of any contingency. This control scheme provides reduced voltage deviations at the converter terminals. The effectiveness of the presented flexible droop regulation scheme has been assessed with MATLAB simulations conducted on a 5-terminal VSC-MTDC framework. Different case studies have been considered to confirm the resilience of the presented droop control methodology.

articleTitle: Accurate Identification of Fault Location for Active Distribution System Using Various Phasor Estimation Methods
abstract: Ensuring a resilient and dependable power supply is becoming progressively more vital in contemporary Active Distribution Systems (ADS). Inclusion of inverter based DGs and nonlinear smart loads causes in waveform distortion reducing the power quality. This increases the error in phasor estimation which is essential in computation of fault location. Further, the infeed current from the other end, due to inverter-based Distributed Generators (IBDGs), increases the error in fault distance computation from the measurement bus. Nevertheless, technological progress in ADS involves the utilization of intelligent smart meters for comprehensive data collection to monitor and improve the reliability. Such an advanced platform has the ability to provide clear picture during the fault which can be utilized to locate the fault. In this work, different phasor estimation techniques; Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Hilbert Transform (HT), Least Square Technique (LSQ) are employed to estimate the phasor which is utilized to compute the differences between pre-fault and post-fault positive, negative, and zero-sequence currents to identify the faulty section. Following that the impedance and reactance is computed using faulty section measurement to find the fault location. Validation of result through the simulation of IEEE 33 bus distribution system in MATLAB/SIMULINK illustrate that the localization percentage error remains within acceptable limit even in the presence of IBDGs an variation in fault resistance.

articleTitle: Securing Smart Grids with Blockchain: Enhancing Data Integrity and Automated Access Control
abstract: The growing integration of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in smart grids has increased their vulnerability to cyber threats. Traditional security measures often struggle to protect against advanced attacks that target the decentralized nature of smart grids. This paper proposes a blockchain-based security framework designed to enhance data integrity and automate access control within smart grids. The framework leverages a permissioned blockchain to ensure scalability and performance while employing smart contracts to enforce security policies in real-time. Key elements include an optimized consensus mechanism for low-latency processing and smart contracts for dynamic security enforcement. Simulation results show an average transaction processing time of 0.0457 seconds, demonstrating the framework's ability to handle a high volume of transactions efficiently. Additionally, the framework achieved a 100% success rate in device authorization and incident response tasks, with zero transaction failures. Gas usage and transaction costs were also maintained at minimal levels, ensuring resource efficiency. These findings indicate that the proposed blockchain-based approach provides a scalable, efficient, and resilient security solution tailored to the dynamic environment of smart grids.

articleTitle: A novel clustering based method for charging infrastructure planning in the context of Indian cities
abstract: Rapid urbanization and increasing environmental concerns have underscored the need for sustainable transportation solutions, with electric vehicles (EVs) being a promising alternative. However, the widespread adoption of EVs is contingent upon the availability of adequate charging infrastructure. This paper presents a novel clustering-based methodology for planning EV charging infrastructure, using K-means clustering and silhouette analysis to categorize cities based on socio-economic and environmental factors, such as EV adoption rates and existing charging points. Each cluster is analyzed to develop a generalized framework for the planning of EV infrastructure, including policy recommendations and infrastructure development strategies. Additionally, specific E V models are assigned to each cluster to optimize infrastructure distribution and promote the growth of the EV ecosystem. This data-driven approach offers customized strategies to improve EV adoption and charging infrastructure, providing valuable information for policymakers, urban planners, and stakeholders working toward sustainable urban mobility.

articleTitle: Minimum Overgeneration Capacity and Net Present Value of Renewable Energy Storage Hybrid System for the electricity demand of 2028-2030 in India
abstract: India must strengthen its electricity grid to accommodate 500 GW of renewables by 2030. To address the variability and intermittency of renewables, a grid-scale energy storage hybrid system would be the key source to balance the rising demand for electricity while ensuring grid stability. Therefore, the primary aim of this manuscript is to determine the optimum overgeneration capacity and minimum net present value required to develop and integrate a solar and wind-based energy storage hybrid system in India comprising of lithium-ion battery and dispatchable generation systems for the electricity demand of 2028-2030 in India. The novelty of the manuscript lies in the methodology adopted, which employs the unmet power demand criteria to determine the techno-economic feasibility and schedule of the aforesaid grid-scale energy storage hybrid system. The methodology adopted in this paper yields a minimum over-generation capacity requirement of 23.55% at a cost of 76.893 GBP/MWh to integrate a 500 MWh LiBESS with the then existing DGS for satisfying the electricity demand of India. The work done in the manuscript can help Indian policymakers revaluate, schedule, refer and decide future energy policies for hybrid grid-scale energy storage systems in India by providing a glimpse of the energy mix when the penetration of solar and wind generators is more than 500 GW by 2030.

Author Keywords: grid-scale lithium-ion battery energy storage system

articleTitle: Advanced Microgrid Planning with EV Charging Stations Using Hybrid Differential Evolution Technique
abstract: Over the past 20 years, the popularity of renewable energy has sharply increased due to environmental concerns. Integrating Distributed Generation (DG) and renewable energy sources, particularly through microgrids, into power distribution systems has become increasingly feasible. Simultaneously, there has been a notable surge in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), driven by environmental initiatives and their advantages over internal combustion engines. Consequently, the planning and management of microgrids within distribution networks have grown increasingly complex. To tackle these complexities, computational evolutionary algorithms have emerged as effective solutions. Among these algorithms, the Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm stands out for its speed and user-friendly simplicity. The proposed work analyzes Hybrid Differential Evolution (HDE) integrated with EV charging infrastructure for microgrid planning. The HDE algorithm combines the power of fuzzy logic and adaptive strategies within the DE framework to address the planning and optimization challenges of microgrids integrated with Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). The paper gives insights into the effectiveness of the HDE algorithm in addressing the challenges related to the planning and operation of microgrids with EV charging stations in modern power systems. Furthermore, the optimization results are compared with those achieved using the DE algorithm.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy Adaptive Differential Evolution optimization algorithm

articleTitle: Scheduling of integrated smart home appliances with conventional loads along with distributed generators
abstract: The increased renewable penetration in the existing grid needs proper scheduling strategy in order to make the optimal usage of the available resources. This has necessitated the proper scheduling of various load users to achieve maximum monetary benefit for the users and operational benefits for the operators. Optimized load scheduling of commercial and integrated smart residential loads in a conventional distribution system is focused majorly to make use of their flexible nature in load scheduling. A scheduling scheme has been proposed with the objective to achieve the maximum cost reduction. This has been analysed with the integration of solar Photo Voltaic based Distributed Generation resources. The concept of load rescheduling is carried with respect to the availability of renewable resources to avoid the grid dependency and to reduce the electrical stress in the system. The proposed methods are tested on IEEE 33 Bus system and the results are promising.

Author Keywords: Operational Cost Minimization Renewable Energy Sources

articleTitle: Carbon Market Scenario: Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Carbon markets play a key role in combating global climate change and aim to achieve a net-zero carbon future. Strong government policy targets and global environmental summits such as the Paris Agreement and the Kyoto Protocol mandate every country to cut greenhouse gas emissions. The carbon market evolving quickly to address the challenges and opportunities involved in achieving carbon neutrality. This paper comprehensively examines various aspects of carbon market intricacies. Additionally, this study presents the current scenario, challenges, and opportunities for the carbon markets, and the carbon credit trading mechanism. Furthermore, the study discusses the steps involved in calculating carbon emissions in detail. The presented study will be helpful in understanding the various aspects of carbon markets and methods to achieve carbon-neutral systems.

articleTitle: Effective Utilization of GNA Margin during Real Time Scheduling of Power
abstract: A new regime of inter-state transmission system (ISTS) planning, allocation of transmission system corridor access, contracting and scheduling of power by buyers including state DISCOMs from sellers and generating stations has been introduced through the implementation of General Network Access (GNA) and Temporary General Network Access (T-GNA) in Indian Power system. These new mechanisms to grant access to ISTS transmission system replaced the old methodologies of transmission planning, corridor allocation and scheduling of power through Long Term Access (LTA), Medium Term Open Access (MTOA) and Short-Term Open Access (STOA). This paper discusses shortcomings of the previous regime and highlights benefits of the new regime. The paper also provides an in-depth analysis of utilization of available GNA margin in real time by a sample state DISCOM in Eastern Region of India. The analysis has been done considering peak hours or the high demand hours of a day for a period of three months when the demand is higher compared to other months of the year. It has been observed through this analysis that there is a scope of effective utilization of real time GNA margin i.e. the quantum of power that can be scheduled by the state DISCOMs under approved GNA quantum in real time over and above the day ahead GNA schedules. The financial benefits in doing so have also been touched upon in the paper.

articleTitle: Self-Healing Schemes in Modern Advanced Power Distribution Networks: An Overview
abstract: The load demand for electrical power has been increasing, continuously, and it may lead to many challenges in providing a secure, stable, and sustained power supply to end users or power consumers. Additionally, this rapid increase in power demand may cause frequent occurrence of interruptions in electricity supply to the end users, which necessitates a systematic approach to mitigate the negative impacts caused by these interruptions. Self-healing and its management techniques provide remedies for such occurrences. This paper presents an overview of self-healing techniques and their management in modern advanced power distribution networks. Furthermore, it also discusses self-healing concepts, current control schemes, solution approaches, and their goals. Moreover, the future research directions that need to be implemented in modern advanced power distribution networks are also described.

articleTitle: Bidding Strategy by using Bi-Level Optimization for Generation Company in Electricity Market and Carbon Emission Rights
abstract: Power companies need to decrease their carbon emissions as part of worldwide efforts to tackle climate change. Companies can achieve this by taking part in a carbon trading system, where they can buy and sell the privilege of emitting a specific amount of carbon. Power firms consider this expense into their business strategy to optimize their electricity and carbon trading strategies by factoring carbon costs' long-term profitability. This model consists of two main components: first, determination of the quantity of carbon credits bought by the generation company at the beginning of the year, second changes in monthly trading volume. With an objective to purchase at a lower price, the model assesses the monthly electricity market bids of the power company. In making judgments, the corporation should consider the remaining carbon credits, the penalty for exceeding the emissions limit, and the competitors' bidding strategies. This model determines the best electricity bid to help the company generate the maximum profit monthly. Simulations show that if the carbon emissions penalty is higher, power companies buy more carbon credits and raise electricity costs. This bi-level model helps power companies coordinate carbon trading and electricity market bids with an aim to balance pollution control and financial performance.

articleTitle: Developed an Optimization Model Using Pyomo to Optimize Water Energy Nexus in Agriculture
abstract: This research focuses on enhancing an individualized water-energy nexus model with particular reference to agricultural use. A solar integrated system is used to drive water pumps for irrigation and household demand. The key aim here is optimizing operational costs associated with power consumption, battery applications, pumping water, and system switching actions. This research achieves a significant reduction in the overall operation cost by using advanced optimization techniques with GNU Linear Programming Kit of a Python-based optimization library (Pyomo). It is an open-source library. A mathematical framework is introduced to improve operational management, incorporating both solar power generation and water requirements to meet agricultural needs. This study also examines the complex switching between inverter sources and battery charging modes in energy storage, emphasizing the need for a balanced approach in managing the water-energy nexus. By improving system switching and storage operations, it advances strategies for sustainable water and energy use. Using Pyomo's flexibility to tackle complex optimization, the study addresses unique challenges in sustainable energy and water systems. The model provides a practical, cost-effective framework for resource management in agriculture, offering valuable insights into sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Neighborhood Digital Twin Energy Models for Demand Load Prediction and Electrification: An Automated Workflow
abstract: This work focuses on automating the conversion of three-dimensional neighborhood digital twin point cloud data to a neighborhood energy model (NEM) for demand load prediction, encompassing loads beyond purely electrical, such as heating oil for space heating. The motivation addresses the common challenge of manually collecting and importing data for energy modeling, particularly at larger scales like neighborhoods. The work aims to establish a workflow to convert digital twin point cloud models to NEMs, facilitating electrification scenarios. Point clouds created with open-source sources, discrete methods and machine learning (ML) methods are used to obtain digital twin neighborhood geometric models. Point cloud data processing includes building footprint extraction through image processing, building height determination using convolutional neural network (CNN) and semantic segmentation networks (SSN), and roof shape identification via regional-based neural network (R-CNN). The process involves creating a workflow in the Rhinoceros environment using Grasshopper, focusing on developing a rapid NEM from a point cloud. The proposed workflow is validated by comparing results with two different energy audits in the case study location, demonstrating its accuracy and reliability. The developed workflow is versatile, and adaptable to various projects by changing input data. It converts digital twin geometric models to energy models. The work reduces the effort and time for urban and energy planners to efficiently conduct energy modeling at a neighborhood scale, enabling the evaluation of net-zero potential and sustainable urban planning. It can also help generate scenarios for the electrification of neighborhoods traditionally served by other energy means. This approach saves time and enhances accuracy in predicting demand loads and exploring electrification pathways, ultimately contributing to more effective and sustainable energy management.

articleTitle: Optimization of Hybrid Biogas-Solar Energy Systems for Sustainable Power Generation in Mauritania
abstract: This paper presents the optimization and performance analysis of hybrid biogas-PV systems for sustainable power generation in Rosso, Mauritania. The study employs HOMER software to model and optimize both on-grid and off-grid configurations, utilizing local data on solar irradiance, biomass availability, and load demand. The most optimal on-grid system configuration includes 801 kW of PV, a 100 kW biogas generator, and a 408 kW converter, achieving a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of $0.041/kWh and a net present cost (NPC) of $1.89M. The off-grid system, with 177 kW of PV, a 100 kW biogas generator, 111 kWh of battery storage, and a 75.8 kW converter, yields an LCOE of $0.128/kWh and an NPC of $830,896. Advanced optimization algorithms, including the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), were applied to further refine the results, with slight LCOE and system size improvements. Environmental impact assessments indicate significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly with the off-grid system. The results highlight the feasibility and economic potential of hybrid biogas-PV systems in Mauritania and similar regions and emphasize the role of renewable energy in achieving sustainable and reliable power generation.

articleTitle: Integrating Blockchain Technology into Smart Grid Systems: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Analyzing the integration of blockchain technology into smart grid systems unveils various opportunities, challenges, and future paths. Combining blockchain with smart grids holds significant potential for transformation, providing improved security, transparency, and effectiveness in managing energy and transactions. Possibilities include enabling peer-to-peer energy trading, optimizing grid operations, and advancing renewable energy integration. Nevertheless, hurdles such as scalability, energy consumption, regulatory uncertainty, and interoperability obstacles need to be overcome to fully utilize blockchain’s capabilities. Moving forward requires collaborative endeavors to create scalable, energy-efficient blockchain solutions, explore novel consensus mechanisms, and establish robust regulatory frameworks conducive to widespread adoption, thus laying the groundwork for a more resilient and sustainable energy ecosystem. However, the integration of blockchain into smart grids also poses several challenges. These include scalability issues, high energy consumption associated with blockchain mining, regulatory uncertainties, interoperability concerns, and the need for consensus mechanisms suitable for energy transactions.

articleTitle: An Overview of Strengthening India’s Carbon Credit System through EV Aggregators
abstract: Decarbonization is vital for mitigating climate change and achieving sustainable development. India’s climate strategy includes the establishment of a domestic carbon market as part of its decarbonization roadmap. Key initiatives include the energy conservation act and the carbon credit trading scheme (CCTS). This paper provides a comprehensive overview of India’s carbon credit mechanisms, with a focus on the role of electric vehicle (EV) aggregators in carbon trading. It explores how EV aggregators can contribute to decarbonization, grid stability, and revenue generation through demand response algorithms and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) integration. Effective implementation requires careful planning to ensure cost-effective decarbonization while maintaining global competitiveness.

articleTitle: Exploring the Feasibility of Hybrid PV-Wind Energy Plant for Costal-Tourism Sites
abstract: This study presents the design, optimization, and performance analysis of a PV-Wind hybrid energy system for Kuakata, a coastal region and popular tourist destination in Bangladesh. The hybrid system integrates Vertical Axis Wind Turbines (VAWT) and photovoltaic (PV) technology, addressing both noise reduction and safety concerns, making it particularly suitable for tourist-friendly environments. The system was optimized using HOMER Pro simulation software, which provided the optimal configuration based on technical, economic, and environmental parameters. The results show a 100% renewable energy fraction, a Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) of $0.041/kWh, and a Net Present Cost (NPC) of $4.58 million. Additionally, the system demonstrates significant environmental benefits by reducing 230,680 kg of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions annually. This study highlights the feasibility of deploying a PV-Wind hybrid system in coastal regions to meet growing energy demands while promoting sustainability and environmental stewardship. The proposed design also enhances the attraction of Kuakata as a tourist destination by offering a quiet and safe renewable energy solution.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Power Flow Analysis Of AC islanded Microgrids For The Identification Of Sensitive Buses
abstract: The growing significance of load flow analysis in microgrids, driven by the increasing integration of Distributed Generators (DGs), has led to the development of various methodologies to address associated challenges. Traditional power flow methods often encounter difficulties in microgrid scenarios due to the lack of a conventional slack bus or reference bus and the dependency of power on frequency, which is influenced by the droop characteristics of DGs. This study presented a Modified Newton-Raphson method specifically tailored for power flow calculations in AC islanded microgrids. The presented modifications enhance convergence and accuracy in the presence of decentralized control mechanisms. To address load uncertainties often overlooked in existing approaches, a Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed. Despite its longstanding use, MCS remains a robust tool for probabilistic analysis, providing a comprehensive assessment of system reliability under varying load conditions. The efficacy of the presented method is validated using a 6-bus test system, where load uncertainties are modeled with normal distribution functions. The analysis reveals the range of voltage variations at each bus across different scenarios, enabling the identification of voltage-sensitive buses. This insight is crucial for optimizing voltage regulation strategies and improving microgrid reliability. A comparison with recent approaches shows the adequate performance of the presented method in terms of exactness and robustness.

articleTitle: Data-driven Modeling of Distribution Network using Experimental Data
abstract: For over three decades the deep learning (DL) has found its applications in modern power systems with introduction and implementation of renewable energy sources (RES) in distributed generation. As RES are integrated in/out of the distribution grids, swift changes in electrical parameters pose a big challenge on power system quality and reliability. To employ an effective monitoring and control, it is needed to represent a system with an equivalent dynamic model, which may be done through DL. DL indicates a multi-layer neural network, which are extremely effective for modeling of non-linear relationships. In this paper, shallow neural networks are realized for a) three phase, and b) dq -frame experimental data, using two different optimization algorithms. The inferences will throw light on effectiveness of difference of log-sum-exp algorithm (DLSEA) as compared to backpropogation algorithm used by neural network toolbox of MATLAB.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Meta-heuristics based Reconfiguration Models to Mitigate Complicated Shadings on Solar PV Arrays
abstract: The enhancement of solar cell efficiency is essential for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems. One major concern is partial shading, leading to power loss and reduced generation. Motivated by various methods available in the literature to handle partial shading issues, this study offers a comprehensive overview of various techniques, categorizing them into five groups: nature-inspired, ancient-inspired, art-inspired, trajectory-inspired, and evolutionary-inspired algorithms. Each algorithm has been evaluated in this study by comparing its performance with established PV array reconfiguration. Additionally, the merits, advantages, disadvantages, challenges, and prospects of various methods, along with future scope, have been explored.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Integration: Real-Time Current Limiting for Grid-Feeding Inverter During LVRT Operation
abstract: The present study delves into the complexities surrounding the integration of renewable energy sources, particularly grid-feeding inverters, into the power system. These inverters are tasked with bolstering grid stability during faulty conditions while maintaining connectivity. A modified fault ridethrough (FRT) methodology is proposed for a grid-linked inverter featuring an inductive filter. This method emphasizes both positive and negative sequence controls to ensure dual current regulation. Adhering to grid code stipulations, the suggested approach involves injecting reactive power during voltage dips and curtailing active power and oscillations at twice the grid frequency. Furthermore, a fresh real-time current limiting approach is introduced, which curbs active power via a closed-loop current magnitude controller to avert inverter tripping. The efficacy of the suggested approach is verified through numerical simulations encompassing various balanced and unbalanced grid fault scenarios. This study makes a substantial contribution to enhancing the dependability and stability of renewable energy systems assimilated into the power grid.

articleTitle: Design of High Voltage and Capacity Electrode for Lithium-ion Battery using Machine Learning
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) present a possible answer in the backdrop of a growing increase in greenhouse gas emissions during the past five decades, primarily due to industries, growing populations and the transport sector. The need for EVs with high ranges necessitates the development of advanced batteries with high capacity and voltage. Conventional approaches, including experimental methods and Density Functional Theory, are accurate but time and resource-intensive. This study leverages machine learning (ML) techniques to supplement these conventional approaches, aiming to rapidly identify high-voltage, high-capacity lithium-ion battery materials crucial for next-generation batteries. Initially, the Materials Project dataset was reduced from 4000 to 2360 instances, setting the stage for enhanced exploration. Applying an Artificial Neural Network model for voltage prediction and clustering algorithms for optimal range identification, the methodology enabled a significant expansion of the original battery database from 2360 to 52000 instances. Within this expanded database, the model revealed 83 potential battery candidates, including 23 unique and novel compounds that had not yet been explored as battery material, thus guiding the design of materials. The results demonstrate a data-driven strategy that expedites the discovery and optimization of battery materials, highlighting the potency of ML in revolutionizing electrochemical energy storage research.

articleTitle: TS-HDBSCAN Based Load Profile Characteristics of Residential Consumers for Demand Response Applications
abstract: Demand response plays a vital role in the electric grid balancing mechanism. The deployment of smart meters motivates residential consumers to participate in demand response programs. Residential consumers have an inherent variability in consumption patterns and have variable shapes, sizes, and densities. The consistency of users' consumption habits over time acts as a vital part of the demand response program. One must analyze the consumers’ load profile characteristics to shift the demand from peak to off-peak hours. Consumers’ consumption behaviors are commonly described using clustering techniques due to the presence of a large number of datasets. However, traditional clustering methods, such as K-means, hierarchical clustering, and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN), are less effective with datasets of varying density. To address this, the time series Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (TS-HDBSCAN) method is proposed for load profile analysis. This approach supports clustering across different shapes, sizes, and densities by creating a condensed hierarchy and selecting clusters based on stability. In this study, the TS-HDBSCAN method is applied to consumption data from 651 residential consumers, demonstrating its suitability for profile selection, classification, and operational stability.

Author Keywords: Time Series Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (TS-HDBSCAN)

articleTitle: Inertia Forecasting for Resilient High-IBR Power Systems using Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RES), particularly inverter-based resources (IBR) like wind and solar, has been reducing system inertia, posing risks to grid stability and potentially leading to cascading outages during power disturbances. This study has examined the impact of these resources on inertia trends and highlights the importance of accurate inertia forecasting for effective grid management. To improve forecasting accuracy, a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) deep learning model has been proposed and was compared with a standard LSTM model using historical data from the Great Britain (GB) power system. Both models were evaluated using key validation metrics, with results indicating that while both forecast inertia effectively, the Bi-LSTM model achieves higher accuracy. This enhanced precision provides grid operators with essential insights for improved grid stability and optimized IBR integration, contributing to a more reliable and sustainable power system.

articleTitle: Generalized Average Modelling & Singular Perturbation Analysis of DAB
abstract: The primary focus of the research is bidirectional DC-DC dual active bridge (DAB) converters, dynamic analysis and comprehensive continuous-time average modelling. It isn't easy to model these converters since the transformer current is completely alternating in nature. A full-order continuous-time average model is proposed, with DC components and first-order terms of transformer current and capacitor voltage serving as state variables. The outcome is a model of the third order when the capacitor's equivalent series resistance (ESR) is ignored and a model of the sixth order when ESR is considered. Specifically for DAB converters, the research constructs a control-to-output-voltage transfer function. It also investigates a unique perturbation analysis in search of circumstances that permit the disentanglement of rapid and slow state variables. According to the experimental data, incorporating the capacitor ESR improves the proposed model's accuracy in predicting the small-signal frequency response.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting Using In-House Algorithm Developed at ERLDC
abstract: India’s fast economic growth is being reflected in its rapidly growing power system. Renewable integration is also taking place at a very high rate matching with India’s commitment for achieving net zero goal [1]. Grid operation is becoming more challenging day by day as variability and uncertainty in the supply side increases. To ensure safe and reliable grid operation, a proper day ahead resource adequacy planning is being performed and made available to operator before actual real time operation. For ensuring resource adequacy on a day ahead basis accurate demand and generation forecasting is extremely essential. While for DISCOMs accurate demand forecasting is essential for portfolio management at the same time, it is equally important for system operators for proper reserve estimation. The electricity demand across various regions of the country exhibits a unique blend of household, agricultural, and industrial load. In the eastern region of the country demand is mainly dominated by domestic load and especially space cooling load [2]. Therefore, it is highly sensitive to weather parameters. This makes accurate forecasting extremely difficult for eastern regional states. Even the most advanced artificial intelligence-based algorithms can sometimes exhibit significant forecasting errors and tuning these complex algorithms in real time by system operators for intraday forecasting becomes difficult. To address this challenge a simple algorithm has been developed in-house at the eastern regional load despatch center. The proposed forecasting algorithm is blend of similar day forecast and heat index based incremental demand estimation. This algorithm exhibits better results and able to capture impact of weather disturbance more accurately than other commonly used methods. In this paper this simple yet effective method has been described for accurate short term load forecasting along with the challenges and way forward.
